definition_zh: 不确定；不确定性；疑虑；未知之事；测量的不确定度；风险与不可预测性
definition_en: the state of not being sure or not being known, and the range within which a measurement or forecast may vary
core_image: 一根指针停在两个刻度之间，微微抖动，既不落在这边也不落在那边
scene: 预报员看着云图，风向在半天之内改了三次，他只能说周末可能下雨也可能不下。The uncertainty in the forecast kept the organizers from booking the outdoor stage.
sceneCN: 这里指预报结果无法确定的状态（第 3 个义项：不可预测、结果未定）；句意为预报中的不确定性让主办方无法预订露天舞台。场景图取象：指针停在两个刻度之间微微抖动。

pos.zh: 不确定；疑虑（不可数，指心理状态）
不确定之事；变数（可数，常用复数）
不确定度（测量学，指结果可能波动的范围）
（经济与管理）不可预测性、风险

derivatives.zh: 不确定的；不肯定的（加表示否定的前缀，指不处于已被判定的状态）
确定性；必然之事（去掉否定前缀后由「已被判定」的形容词加名词词尾构成）
确定的；某个的（由拉丁语「已判定」义而来，经由表示「筛定」的动词）
没有把握地；迟疑地（在形容词后加副词词尾）

senses.title: Not knowing for sure
senses.definition: the state of not knowing whether something is true or what will happen
senses.definitionCN: 不知道某事是否为真、或将会如何的状态
senses.example: Her uncertainty about the answer was obvious.
senses.exampleCN: 她对答案没有把握，这一点很明显。
senses.why: The word negates a Latin adjective meaning settled, so it names the condition of not being settled.
senses.whyCN: 这个词否定了一个意为「已判定」的拉丁形容词，因此指未被定下来的状态。

senses.title: Something not yet decided
senses.definition: a matter whose outcome is not yet fixed, often counted in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 结果尚未确定的事情，常用复数计数
senses.example: The plan has too many uncertainties to price.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划变数太多，无法定价。
senses.why: Uncertainty can be a thing as well as a mood, and business counts the things rather than the mood.
senses.whyCN: 不确定性既能是心情，也能是事情，商界数的是事情而非心情。

senses.title: What cannot be predicted
senses.definition: the part of a situation that cannot be forecast, as in weather or markets
senses.definitionCN: 局面中无法预报的部分，如天气或市场中的情形
senses.example: The uncertainty in the forecast kept the organizers from booking the outdoor stage.
senses.exampleCN: 预报中的不确定性让主办方无法预订露天舞台。
senses.why: Forecasting separates what is known from what remains open, and the open part takes this name.
senses.whyCN: 预报把已知与仍未定的部分分开，仍未定的那部分就用这个名字。

senses.title: The spread of a measurement
senses.definition: the range within which the true value of a measurement is expected to lie
senses.definitionCN: 测量的真值预期落在其中的范围
senses.example: The result was reported with an uncertainty of two per cent.
senses.exampleCN: 结果报告时附有百分之二的不确定度。
senses.why: Metrology refuses to give a bare number; every figure comes with the width of its doubt.
senses.whyCN: 计量学不肯给出光秃秃的数字，每个数都带着它那份怀疑的宽度。

senses.title: The quantum limit
senses.definition: the limit on how precisely certain paired properties of a particle can be known at once
senses.definitionCN: 粒子的某些成对属性无法同时被测得足够精确的限度
senses.example: The uncertainty principle is about knowledge, not about laboratory clumsiness.
senses.exampleCN: 不确定性原理讲的是知识限度，而不是实验室笨手笨脚。
senses.why: Physics found a doubt built into nature itself, and borrowed the everyday word for it.
senses.whyCN: 物理学发现怀疑被造进了自然本身，于是借用了日常的词来称它。

senses.title: Economic unpredictability
senses.definition: unpredictability in prices, demand or policy that makes planning difficult
senses.definitionCN: 价格、需求或政策上的不可预测，使规划变得困难
senses.example: Uncertainty over tariffs froze new investment.
senses.exampleCN: 关税上的不确定让新投资停滞。
senses.why: Firms do not react to bad news so much as to not knowing, which is why the word dominates economics.
senses.whyCN: 企业反应的与其说是坏消息，不如说是「不知道」，所以这个词在经济领域举足轻重。

senses.title: Hesitation in a person
senses.definition: a feeling of doubt that makes a person hesitate or speak cautiously
senses.definitionCN: 使人迟疑或说话谨慎的怀疑感
senses.example: He answered with a slight uncertainty in his voice.
senses.exampleCN: 他回答时声音里带着一点迟疑。
senses.why: The inner sense is the oldest: an unsettled judgement shows in the voice before it shows in the data.
senses.whyCN: 内心的义项最古老：未定的判断先露在声音里，然后才露在数据里。

senses.title: Risk that cannot be counted
senses.definition: a situation whose probabilities are unknown, distinguished from risk in which odds can be assigned
senses.definitionCN: 概率未知的处境，与可以给出赔率的「风险」相区别
senses.example: Decision theory separates uncertainty from measurable risk.
senses.exampleCN: 决策理论把不确定性与可计量的风险分开。
senses.why: If the odds are known it is risk; if they are not, it is uncertainty, and the distinction matters to insurers.
senses.whyCN: 赔率已知的是风险，未知的是不确定性，这一区分对保险业至关重要。

senses.title: The open future
senses.definition: the general condition of the future being undecided, a theme in philosophy and literature
senses.definitionCN: 未来尚未定局的一般状况，是哲学与文学的常见主题
senses.example: The novel turns uncertainty into a kind of freedom.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说把不确定变成了一种自由。
senses.why: If the future were closed, choice would be pointless; the word can name that openness rather than a lack.
senses.whyCN: 若未来已经闭合，选择便无意义；这个词也能指那种敞开，而不只是一种缺失。

intro.en: Uncertainty is the negative of certainty, from Latin certus 'settled', itself from cernere 'to sift, to decide'. The root history is generally accepted; only the exact date of the English noun is uncertain.
intro.cn: uncertainty 是 certainty 的否定形式，certainty 出自拉丁语 certus「已定的」，而 certus 又出自 cernere「筛、判定」。词根历史一般认为可靠，只有这个英语名词的确切年代不确定。

items.en: Cernere meant to sift or to separate, and from sifting came the sense of deciding a matter.
items.cn: cernere 意为筛、分开，从筛选中引出判定一件事的意思。

items.en: Certus meant settled or decided, said of a thing no longer in doubt.
items.cn: certus 意为已定、已决，用于不再有疑问之事。

items.en: Latin added the negative prefix to make incertus, not settled, the direct ancestor of uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语加上否定前缀构成 incertus「未定的」，正是 uncertain 的直接祖先。

items.en: Old French uncertain and the noun forme carried the word into English in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 古法语的形式把这个词与名词形态在中世纪带入英语。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the word was given a numeric sense, the band around a measured value.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪，这个词获得数量含义，指测量值周围的那一条带。

items.en: Quantum theory and modern finance both made uncertainty a technical quantity, one in nature and one in markets.
items.cn: 量子理论与现代金融都把不确定性做成了技术量，一个在自然里，一个在市场里。

note.en: The first group shares the settled root or looks similar; the second group names neighbouring states that are often folded into uncertainty.
note.cn: 第一组或共享「已定」词根，或字形相近；第二组是常被并入「不确定性」的邻近状态。

entries.definition: The adjective: not sure, not settled.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：不确定的、未定的。

entries.definition: The positive noun: the state of being settled.
entries.definitionCN: 肯定形式的名词：已被确定的状态。

entries.definition: A feeling of complete sureness, usually subjective.
entries.definitionCN: 完全的确定感，通常指主观上的。

entries.definition: To find out for certain; it shares cernere but not the negative prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 查明、确定；共享「筛定」词根，不含否定前缀。

entries.definition: Strange in a way that unsettles; it looks like the same negative but comes from ken, knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 怪得令人不安；看似同一否定前缀，其实出自表示「知晓」的词。

entries.definition: A feeling of not being convinced, the personal side of uncertainty.
entries.definitionCN: 未被说服的感觉，是不确定性在个人身上的那一面。

entries.definition: Having more than one possible meaning, a property of statements rather than of the future.
entries.definitionCN: 存在不止一种可能含义，是陈述的属性而非未来的属性。

entries.definition: Exposure to a loss whose probability can be estimated.
entries.definitionCN: 暴露于损失之中，而其概率可以估算。

entries.definition: The tendency of a quantity to change, which produces uncertainty in measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 数量容易变动的倾向，正是它造成测量上的不确定。

entries.definition: The rate at which prices swing, a market measure of uncertainty.
entries.definitionCN: 价格摆动的幅度，是市场对不确定性的度量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real sifting root, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「筛定」词根、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Certain comes from a Latin verb meaning to sift, so certainty is what survives the sieve and uncertainty is what does not.
normal.cn: certain 出自意为「筛」的拉丁动词，确定性是筛后留下之物，不确定性是没留下的。

normal.en: The family pairs neatly: certain and certainty against uncertain and uncertainty.
normal.cn: 同族词成对出现：确定的、确定性，对不确定的、不确定性。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: measurement uncertainty, economic uncertainty, the uncertainty principle.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：测量不确定度、经济不确定性、不确定性原理。

normal.en: In decision theory risk has countable odds, uncertainty does not.
normal.cn: 在决策理论里，风险有可数的赔率，不确定性没有。

normal.en: The plural uncertainties names concrete open questions, not a mood.
normal.cn: 复数形式指一件件还没定的事，而不是一种心情。

abstract.en: Uncertainty is the space in which a decision is still a decision.
abstract.cn: 不确定性是那块空间，决定在其中还算得上决定。

abstract.en: A number without an uncertainty is a claim pretending to be a fact.
abstract.cn: 没有不确定度的数字，是假装成事实的主张。

abstract.en: Uncertainty is not the enemy of knowledge; it is the shape knowledge takes at its edges.
abstract.cn: 不确定性不是知识的敌人，而是知识在边缘处呈现的形状。

examples.en: Uncertainty about the funding delayed the whole project.
examples.cn: 资金上的不确定拖住了整个项目。

examples.en: Every measurement carries an uncertainty that must be stated.
examples.cn: 每次测量都带有必须说明的不确定度。

examples.en: She learned to work despite the uncertainty of the outcome.
examples.cn: 她学会了在结果未定之时照样做事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「安色滕提」——心里那根针迟迟不落定：不确定

root: certainty 的否定形式；certain 出自拉丁语 certus「已定」← cernere「筛、判定」，加否定前缀构成 incertus「未定」，经古法语进入英语。二十世纪起在测量学、量子物理与金融中获得技术含义。名词进入英语的确切年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from a private doubt to a public quantity: not knowing, an open question, an unpredictable part, the spread of a measurement, the quantum limit, economic unpredictability, personal hesitation, uncountable risk, and the openness of the future.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从私人的疑虑走到公共的量：拿不准、尚未定的事、无法预测的部分、测量的不确定度、量子限度、经济上的不可预测、个人的迟疑、无法计数的风险，以及未来的敞开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle resting between two marks and trembling, belonging to neither.
core.cn: 核心意象：指针停在两个刻度之间微微抖动，哪一边都不属于。

branches.en: THE UNSETTLED MIND: a judgement not yet made, showing as hesitation in a voice.
branches.cn: 未定的心：尚未作出的判断，先从声音里的迟疑露出来。

branches.en: THE OPEN QUESTION: a matter whose outcome is still unfixed and can be counted.
branches.cn: 未决的问题：结果尚未确定、还可以数出来的一件事。

branches.en: THE UNFORECASTABLE: weather that may or may not hold, tariffs that may or may not change.
branches.cn: 无法预报之物：可能下也可能不下的雨，可能改也可能不改的关税。

branches.en: THE WIDTH OF A NUMBER: the band around a measured value, and the quantum limit on knowing two things at once.
branches.cn: 数字的宽度：测量值周围那一条带，以及同时知道两件事的量子限度。

branches.en: THE OPEN FUTURE: risk without countable odds, and the freedom of a future not yet closed.
branches.cn: 敞开的未来：没有可数赔率的风险，以及尚未闭合的未来的自由。

intro.en: Uncertainty negates a Latin adjective of settledness and turns it into an abstract noun.
intro.cn: uncertainty 否定一个表示「已定」的拉丁形容词，并把它变成抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: The base is certus from cernere, with the negative prefix and the noun ending added in turn.
latinIntro.cn: 基础是出自 cernere 的 certus，先后加上否定前缀与名词词尾。

items.example: The noun covers both a mood and a measured range.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既指心情，也指测量出的范围。
它把确定的变成不确定的。

它构成确定性与不确定性。

items.example: The adjective also means a particular one.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词也有「某一个」的意思。

items.example: The pair makes a clean positive and negative.
items.exampleCN: 这一对构成干净的正与负。

items.example: It shares the root without the negative.
items.exampleCN: 它共享词根，却没有否定。

items.example: The noun names the feeling rather than the fact.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指感觉而非事实。

latinEntries.example: Latin incertus means not settled, doubtful.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 incertus 意为未定的、可疑的。

latinEntries.example: Latin certus means settled or sure.

definition_zh: 揭开；掀开；发现；揭露；查明
definition_en: to remove a cover, or to find out something that was hidden
core_image: 把盖布一把掀开，底下原本藏着的东西露在光里
scene: 考古队在沙地里刮了一上午，终于露出半块刻着字的石板边缘。The reporter uncovered a series of secret payments.
sceneCN: 这里 uncover 是「发现、揭露」（第 2 个义项：把藏起来的事查出来）；句意为记者揭露了一连串秘密付款。掀开盖布让底下露出来，正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 动词分词作形容词，义为「无遮盖的；被揭发的」
动词加 -ing 构成名词，义为「揭露；发掘」
同源近义词，义为「发现」

senses.title: To take a cover off something
senses.definition: to lift or remove the thing lying over an object
senses.definitionCN: 把盖在某物上面的东西提起或拿走
senses.example: He uncovered the pot to let the steam out.
senses.exampleCN: 他把锅盖揭开让蒸汽散出去。
senses.why: The verb is un- plus cover, so it simply undoes the covering.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是 un- 加 cover，就是把「盖」这个动作反过来。

senses.title: To find out something hidden
senses.definition: to discover a fact or plan that someone wanted concealed
senses.definitionCN: 发现某人本想隐瞒的事实或计划
senses.example: The audit uncovered serious errors.
senses.exampleCN: 审计查出了严重错误。
senses.why: Once the cover is physically lifted, the figurative cover of secrecy behaves the same way.
senses.whyCN: 盖布既然能被掀开，机密这层盖布也一样。

senses.title: To make a truth public
senses.definition: to bring a hidden wrongdoing into public view
senses.definitionCN: 使隐秘的恶行进入公众视野
senses.example: Two journalists uncovered the whole scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 两名记者揭发了整个计划。
senses.why: Muckrakers and auditors alike use the word once the covering image is in place.
senses.whyCN: 只要「盖布」这个比喻立住了，扒粪记者与审计员都会用这个词。

senses.title: To show a hidden part naturally
senses.definition: of natural forces, to leave something visible by moving what lies over it
senses.definitionCN: 指自然力量把覆盖之物移开，使某物可见
senses.example: The rain uncovered the old stone path.
senses.exampleCN: 这场雨把那条古老的石板路冲了出来。
senses.why: Water and wind do the uncovering without any intention at all.
senses.whyCN: 风雨本无意图，却完成了揭开这件事。

senses.title: To leave oneself unprotected
senses.definition: to put a body or a position in the open with no shield
senses.definitionCN: 把身体或阵地放在毫无遮挡之处
senses.example: The soldiers edged forward, uncovered by any wall.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们向前挪动，没有任何墙作掩护。
senses.why: To have no cover is to be uncovered, so the military sense is the literal picture standing alone.
senses.whyCN: 没有掩护就是无遮盖，因此这个军事义只是把字面画面单独摆出来。

intro.en: The word is built in English from un- and cover, whose ultimate source is Latin.
intro.cn: 这个词在英语里由 un- 与 cover 组合而成，而 cover 的源头是拉丁语。

items.en: Cooperire joins com-, fully, and operire, to close or hide, meaning to cover completely.
items.cn: cooperire 由 com-（完全）与 operire（关闭、遮盖）组成，意为完全盖住。

items.en: Old French covrir and a shorter form give English cover.
items.cn: 古法语 covrir 及其较短形式给英语带来 cover。

items.en: Cover appears in English in the twelfth century with the sense of covering a thing.
items.cn: cover 在十二世纪进入英语，意为盖住某物。

items.en: Uncover is formed by plain prefixing, first for physical lifting.
items.cn: uncover 由简单加前缀构成，最初用于实物掀盖。

items.en: From the nineteenth century it is common for exposing scandals.
items.cn: 十九世纪起，用它来指揭发丑闻变得常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cover stem, and the near-meaning group gathers verbs of disclosure.
note.cn: 形近组共用 cover 词干，近义组汇集表示揭露的动词。

normalIntro.en: The word is simply the undo of covering, first of pots and then of secrets.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词不过是「盖」的反动作，先掀锅盖，再掀秘密。

normal.en: Un- plus cover reads as take the cover off, exactly as its letters suggest.
normal.cn: un- 加 cover 读作把盖拿走，正如字面所写。

normal.en: Discover and uncover both build on the same Latin root of hiding.
normal.cn: discover 与 uncover 同建在一个表示「遮盖」的拉丁词根上。

normal.en: Uncovered is also an adjective for a field with nothing over it.
normal.cn: uncovered 也可作形容词，指没有遮盖的空地。

normal.en: Journalists uncover schemes; engineers uncover faults in a design.
normal.cn: 记者揭露阴谋，工程师查设计里的缺陷。

normal.en: The past tense is uncovered, a regular -ed form.
normal.cn: 过去式是 uncovered，规则的加 -ed 形式。

abstract.en: Take a corner of the cloth and lift it in one motion.
abstract.cn: 捏住盖布一角，一下掀起来。

abstract.en: See beneath it something already there, only unknown.
abstract.cn: 看见底下早就在，只是没人知道。

abstract.en: Then watch rain wash soil off an old stone path.
abstract.cn: 再看雨水冲掉石板路上的泥土。

examples.en: The police uncovered a network of false documents.
examples.cn: 警方查出了一个假证件网络。

examples.en: Wind had uncovered the roots of the fallen tree.
examples.cn: 风把倒下的树的根露了出来。

examples.en: She uncovered the tray to show us the cake.
examples.cn: 她把托盘盖掀开，让我们看那块蛋糕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安卡佛」——安好盖子再卡上，一掀开，佛就现身了。

root: un-（反向前缀）+ cover（古法语 covrir，源自拉丁语 cooperire，由 com-「完全」+ operire「遮盖」构成）

sensesIntro.en: All senses undo a covering, whether a lid, a secrecy, a layer of soil, or a shield.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都在解除一层遮盖：锅盖、保密、土层，或掩护。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cloth pulled back from what lay beneath.
core.cn: 核心意象：盖布被掀开，露出底下的东西。

branches.en: The physical branch: pots, trays, and lids.
branches.cn: 实物分支：锅、托盘与盖子。

branches.en: The inquiry branch: audits and police work that find facts.
branches.cn: 调查分支：审计与侦查查出事实。

branches.en: The public branch: reporters exposing a scheme.
branches.cn: 公开分支：记者揭发阴谋。

branches.en: The nature branch: rain and wind uncovering stone.
branches.cn: 自然分支：风雨冲露出石板。

branches.en: The military branch, where no wall gives cover.
branches.cn: 军事分支：没有墙可作掩护。

intro.en: A reversing prefix on a verb of hiding, itself from Latin.
intro.cn: 反向前缀盖在一个表示遮盖的动词上，该动词源自拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: Operire, to close, also lies behind cover, covert, and discover.
latinIntro.cn: operire（关闭）还支撑着 cover、covert、discover。

items.exampleCN: uncover 是 cover 的反动作。

items.example: The boat stood uncovered all winter.
items.exampleCN: 那条船整个冬天都露天放着。

items.example: The uncovering of the tomb took years.
items.exampleCN: 这座墓的发掘花了好几年。

definition_zh: 经历；经受；承受；（医）接受（治疗、手术）
definition_en: to go through something difficult or a process that changes you
core_image: 一个人低头走进一条昏暗的通道，出来时已经不同了
scene: 手术室外的长椅上，家属们安静地等着，护士说病人正在里面接受一次大手术。She had to undergo two operations in one year.
sceneCN: 这里 undergo 是「接受（手术）」（第 3 个义项：承受某种过程）；句意为她一年里不得不接受两次手术。低头走进昏暗通道，出来时已不同，正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 过去分词，义为「已经历」
过去式，义为「经历了」
现在分词，义为「正在经历」

senses.title: To go through an experience
senses.definition: to pass through a period or an event that acts on you
senses.definitionCN: 穿过一段时期或一件事，并受其作用
senses.example: The town underwent great changes in the war.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城在战争中经历了巨大变化。
senses.why: Under means beneath and go means move, so to undergo is to pass beneath a weight and come out the other side.
senses.whyCN: under 意为在其下，go 意为行进，合起来就是从那重压底下穿过、再从另一头出来。

senses.title: To be subjected to a process
senses.definition: to be put through a process such as testing or repair
senses.definitionCN: 被放入检查、修理之类的流程中
senses.example: Every engine undergoes a final check.
senses.exampleCN: 每台发动机都要经过最后检查。
senses.why: A process laid over you is a weight over you, and the two images meet.
senses.whyCN: 加在你身上的一套流程就是压在你身上的一重压，两个意象在此汇合。

senses.title: To receive medical treatment
senses.definition: to have a treatment performed on one’s body
senses.definitionCN: 让人在自己身体上施行某项治疗
senses.example: He underwent a heart operation last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 去年春天他接受了一次心脏手术。
senses.why: In medicine the word keeps the sense of letting something heavy pass over the body.
senses.whyCN: 在医学里，这个词保留了「让沉重之物从身体上经过」的意思。

senses.title: To endure hardship or suffering
senses.definition: to bear pain or loss over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间里承受疼痛或损失
senses.example: The villagers underwent years of shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们过了好几年短缺的日子。
senses.why: Hardship is a weight that stays on for a long time, and the word names the bearing of it.
senses.whyCN: 艰难是长时间压着的一副重量，这个词指的正是把它担过去。

senses.title: To suffer a change of state
senses.definition: of a thing, to pass into a different state through a process
senses.definitionCN: 指某物经由过程转入另一种状态
senses.example: The metal undergoes expansion when heated.
senses.exampleCN: 金属受热时会发生膨胀。
senses.why: Whatever the process is, the subject comes out different, which is why the word suits changes.
senses.whyCN: 不论过程为何，主体走过之后都会变样，所以它特别适合说变化。

intro.en: The word is an English compound of under and go, first recorded in Old English.
intro.cn: 这个词是 under 与 go 的英语复合词，最早见于古英语。

items.en: Undergan means to undergo or to undertake, built from under and gan, to go.
items.cn: undergān 意为承受或着手，由 under 与 gān（走）构成。

items.en: The prefix under carried the idea of coming under something.
items.cn: 前缀 under 带着「进到某物之下」的意思。

items.en: Middle English undergon keeps the sense of passing through hardship.
items.cn: 中古英语 undergon 保留「穿过艰难」之义。

items.en: The past forms underwent and undergone settle into their modern spelling.
items.cn: 过去式与过去分词定型为 underwent 与 undergone。

items.en: Medical usage for treatment grows in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 表示「接受治疗」的医学用法在十九、二十世纪兴盛。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers under- compounds, and the near-meaning group collects verbs of experiencing.
note.cn: 形近组汇集 under- 复合词，近义组汇集表示经历的动词。

entries.definition: to take on a duty or task
to weaken quietly from below
to lie beneath as a cause
to live through an event
to bear pain patiently
to feel pain or loss
to keep away from

normalIntro.en: Under plus go: you go beneath a thing and come out on the far side.
normalIntro.cn: under 加 go：从一件东西底下走过去，再从另一头出来。

normal.en: Undergo is irregular: underwent today, undergone in the past participle.
normal.cn: undergo 不规则：过去式 underwent，过去分词 undergone。

normal.en: The word almost always takes an article with a process, as in undergo an operation.
normal.cn: 这个词接过程名词时通常带冠词，如 undergo an operation。

normal.en: Undertake takes on a duty, while undergo receives an experience.
normal.cn: undertake 是主动承担，undergo 是被动承受。

normal.en: Hospitals use it constantly: patients undergo tests, scans, and surgery.
normal.cn: 医院里用得极多：病人 undergo 检查、扫描、手术。

normal.en: Undergo change is the standard formal way to say something was altered.
normal.cn: undergo change 是表示「发生了变化」的正式说法。

abstract.en: Step down into a dim passage and keep walking.
abstract.cn: 低头走进一条昏暗的通道，一直往前走。

abstract.en: Feel the walls close while your own shape changes.
abstract.cn: 感觉两侧墙收拢，而你自己的形状在变。

abstract.en: Come out at the other end wearing that change.
abstract.cn: 从另一头出来时，已经带着那层变化。

examples.en: The bridge will undergo repairs this summer.
examples.cn: 这座桥今年夏天将进行维修。

examples.en: Patients must undergo a full examination first.
examples.cn: 病人必须先接受全面检查。

examples.en: The old factory underwent a complete change of use.
examples.cn: 那座旧厂房经历了彻底的用途改变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安得够」——能不能安得够稳，只看你经不经得住这一程。

root: 古英语 under（在下）+ gān（走），undergān 意为承受、着手；过去式 underwent，过去分词 undergone

sensesIntro.en: In every sense the subject passes beneath something, an event, a process, an operation, or hardship.
sensesIntro.cn: 在每一个义项里，主体都从某样东西底下经过：一件事、一套流程、一次手术，或一段艰难。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: walking through a dim passage and changing inside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：穿过昏暗通道，在里面被改变。

branches.en: The change branch: events and heat that alter the subject.
branches.cn: 变化分支：改变主体的事件与热。

branches.en: The process branch: checks and repairs laid over a thing.
branches.cn: 流程分支：加在物上的检查与修理。

branches.en: The medical branch: operations and scans on the body.
branches.cn: 医学分支：在身体上做的手术与扫描。

branches.en: The hardship branch: years of shortage borne quietly.
branches.cn: 艰难分支：默默承受的多年短缺。

branches.en: The common sense of living through a period.
branches.cn: 常用义：度过一段时期。

intro.en: Two Old English pieces joined: a preposition of position and a verb of moving.
intro.cn: 两块古英语部件拼合：一个方位介词与一个走动的动词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source, so the Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 此词没有拉丁语来源，故拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.exampleCN: 信任是这笔交易的基础。

definition_zh: 本科生；大学生；（作定语）本科的
definition_en: a student at a university who has not yet taken a first degree
core_image: 阶梯上还没拿到第一块牌子的那个年轻人
scene: 九月开学，图书馆门前排着长队，手里拿着新学生证的都是刚入学的年轻人。She was still an undergraduate when she wrote her first book.
sceneCN: 这里 undergraduate 是「本科生」（第 1 个义项：尚未取得学位的大学生）；句意为她写第一本书时还是本科生。还没拿到第一块牌子的年轻人，正是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 形容词：本科的；大学生的

derivatives.zh: 去掉前缀的原词，义为「毕业生；研究生」
口语缩略形式，义为「本科生」
复合形容词，义为「本科层次的」

senses.title: A student without a first degree
senses.definition: a student working toward a bachelor’s degree
senses.definitionCN: 正在攻读学士学位的学生
senses.example: The lab takes two undergraduates each summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这个实验室每年夏天招收两名本科生。
senses.why: Graduare in Latin means to take a step, and gradus is a step; under marks the stage below the degree step.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 graduare 意为迈一步，gradus 是台阶；under 标记学位那一级之下的阶段。

senses.title: A student at a college in the first cycle
senses.definition: a person at college in their first course of higher study
senses.definitionCN: 在大学第一级课程中就读的人
senses.example: Undergraduates here live in colleges, not flats.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的大学生住在学院里，而不在校外公寓。
senses.why: British universities above all use the word to separate students from postgraduates on the same campus.
senses.whyCN: 尤以英国大学如此，用这个词把同一校园里的本科生与研究生区分开。

senses.title: Study at the first level
senses.definition: used before nouns for courses and degrees below master’s level
senses.definitionCN: 用于硕士水平以下的课程与学位名词之前
senses.example: She teaches an undergraduate seminar on poetry.
senses.exampleCN: 她教一门本科诗歌研讨课。
senses.why: The noun freely becomes a label for the whole level of study.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词又自由地转作整个学习阶段的标签。

senses.title: A part that is still in progress
senses.titleCN: 尚未完成本科阶段的人
senses.definition: a person whose degree is not yet awarded and so not yet a graduate
senses.definitionCN: 学位尚未授予、因而还不算 graduate 的人
senses.example: He is an undergraduate until the results come out.
senses.exampleCN: 成绩公布之前他还算本科生。
senses.why: The prefix is a status marker: the step has not been taken yet.
senses.whyCN: 前缀是个身份标记：那一步还没有迈出去。

senses.title: A young member of a learned community
senses.definition: in older usage, a beginning student within a college
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法中指学院里刚开始学习的人
senses.example: In 1820 the college had forty undergraduates.
senses.exampleCN: 1820 年这所学院有四十名在读学生。
senses.why: In that older world the word simply placed a beginner at the foot of the college ladder.
senses.whyCN: 在那个更早的世界里，这个词只是把一个初学者放在学院梯子的最下一级。

intro.en: The word is a Latin step, with an English prefix marking the stage below it.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语的「一步」，加英语前缀标记那一步之下的阶段。

items.en: Gradus means a step or a degree, and gradus honoris is an academic degree.
items.cn: gradus 意为台阶或等级，gradus honoris 即学位。

items.en: Graduare means to take a degree, and the medieval university is its stage.
items.cn: graduare 意为取得学位，其舞台就是中世纪大学。

items.en: The noun graduate enters English from that academic sense.
items.cn: graduate 由这层学术义进入英语。

items.en: Undergraduate is formed with the prefix to name students below the degree step.
items.cn: 加上前缀构成 undergraduate，指位于学位台阶之下的学生。

items.en: The Oxford and Cambridge systems fix the British usage in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪牛津与剑桥的制度把英式用法固定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the grad- stem of steps and degrees, and the near-meaning group names student roles.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示台阶与学位的 grad- 词干，近义组列出学生身份。

entries.definition: a person who has a degree
the ceremony of taking a degree
a step on a scale
a student beyond a first degree
a person who studies
a first-year student
a student in the final year

normalIntro.en: Gradus is a step, so an undergraduate has not yet stepped onto the degree level.
normalIntro.cn: gradus 是台阶，undergraduate 就是还没踏上学位那一级的人。

normal.en: Graduate means the step has been taken, and undergraduate means it has not.
normal.cn: graduate 表示已迈上那一步，undergraduate 表示还没迈上。

normal.en: Grade and gradual come from the same step, one a rank, one a pace.
normal.cn: grade 与 gradual 同出这一步，一个是等级，一个是步伐。

normal.en: In British use undergraduates are at college, while postgraduates remain after the degree.
normal.cn: 英式用法里本科生在学院读书，postgraduate 是拿过学位后继续读的人。

normal.en: Undergrad is the joking short form heard on campus.
normal.cn: 校园里常听到打趣的缩略说法 undergrad。

normal.en: The plural undergraduates is regular, with no change of the stem.
normal.cn: 复数 undergraduates 规则变化，词干不变。

abstract.en: See a staircase with the degree marked one step higher.
abstract.cn: 看见一段楼梯，学位那一级标得更高一点。

abstract.en: Watch a young person standing one step below it with books.
abstract.cn: 看一个年轻人抱着书站在它下面一级。

abstract.en: Notice that the sign on that step never names the person, only the gap.
abstract.cn: 注意那一级上的标牌并不叫出人名，只标出这段差距。

examples.en: Most undergraduates live on campus in their first year.
examples.cn: 大多数本科生第一年住在校内。

examples.en: He completed an undergraduate degree in economics.
examples.cn: 他修完了经济学本科学位。

examples.en: The journal is written for undergraduates, not specialists.
examples.cn: 这份刊物是给本科生而不是专家看的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安得瓜爵特」——还没安得上学位这顶「爵」帽，所以只能叫本科生。

root: under-（在……之下）+ graduate（拉丁语 gradus「台阶、等级」→ graduare「取得学位」）；同族有 grade、graduation、postgraduate

sensesIntro.en: The word marks a place on a staircase: below the step where a degree is taken.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词标记楼梯上的位置：在授予学位那一级之下。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a young person standing one step below the degree.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个年轻人站在学位那一级的下方。

branches.en: The person branch: the student working toward a degree.
branches.cn: 人分支：正在攻读学位的学生。

branches.en: The labelling branch: courses, degrees, and journals.
branches.cn: 标签分支：课程、学位与刊物。

branches.en: The status branch: not yet counted among graduates.
branches.cn: 身份分支：还不在毕业生之列。

branches.en: The older branch: a beginning member of a college.
branches.cn: 旧义分支：学院里初入门的人。

branches.en: The plain campus sense heard every September.
branches.cn: 每年九月都能听到的校园义。

intro.en: An English prefix on a Latin word for a step.
intro.cn: 英语前缀加在表示「台阶」的拉丁词上。

latinIntro.en: The grad- root of steps also gives grade, gradual, and progress.
latinIntro.cn: 表示台阶的 grad- 词根还生出 grade、gradual、progress。

items.example: Under- marks the stage below a degree.
items.exampleCN: under- 标记学位之下的一级。

items.example: Graduare means to take a degree.
Undergraduate names the person at that stage.
items.exampleCN: undergraduate 指处于该阶段的人。

definition_zh: 地下的；秘密的；地下组织；（英）地铁
definition_en: below the surface of the ground, or hidden from public view
core_image: 在土层之下，一条亮着灯的线路悄悄延伸
scene: 冬天地面结着薄冰，人们缩着脖子下到楼梯深处，那里暖风阵阵、车灯闪动。They took the underground across the city.
sceneCN: 这里 underground 是「地铁（英式）」（第 2 个义项：地下的交通系统）；句意为他们乘地铁穿城而过。土层下亮灯延伸的线路，正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 去掉前缀的原词，义为「地面；场地」
复合名词加 -er，义为「地下工作者」
美式同义词，义为「地铁」

senses.title: Below the surface of the earth
senses.definition: placed or happening under the surface of the ground
senses.definitionCN: 位于或发生于地表之下
senses.example: The city built a huge underground car park.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市建了一个巨大的地下停车场。
senses.why: Ground is the surface we stand on, and under puts the whole system beneath it.
senses.whyCN: ground 是我们脚下的地表，under 把整套东西放到它下面。

senses.title: A city railway below the streets
senses.definition: the railway system that runs in tunnels under a city
senses.definitionCN: 在城市街道下方的隧道中运行的铁路系统
senses.example: The underground is quicker than the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 地铁比公交车快。
senses.why: Londoners shortened the full name to the underground, and the noun took over.
senses.whyCN: 伦敦人把这套系统的全名缩作 the underground，名词就此定型。

senses.title: Hidden and against the authorities
senses.definition: of a movement or publication, operating in secret against a government
senses.definitionCN: 指运动或出版物在暗处与政府对抗
senses.example: The novel was passed around in underground copies.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说以地下本的形式流传。
senses.why: To operate underground is literally to be out of sight, and secrecy borrows the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 在地下活动字面上就是见不到光，秘密也就借用了这张图。

senses.title: To go into hiding
senses.definition: of a person or group, to disappear from public life
senses.definitionCN: 指人或团体从公众生活中消失
senses.example: The writer went underground for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 这位作家隐没了十年。
senses.why: When someone sinks below the surface, they can no longer be found by ordinary means.
senses.whyCN: 一个人沉到地表之下，常规手段就找不到他了。

senses.title: Secret and unofficial
senses.definition: existing in secret without official approval
senses.definitionCN: 未经官方许可而在暗中存在的
senses.example: An underground economy grew along the border.
senses.exampleCN: 边境上长出了一片地下经济。
senses.why: Money that never enters the books lives, in effect, below the visible streets.
senses.whyCN: 从不进账的钱，实际上就生活在看得见的街道下面。

intro.en: The word is an English combination of a preposition and a noun of the earth.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语介词与表示地面的名词的组合。

items.en: Grund means the bottom or the ground, and under carries the sense of beneath.
items.cn: grund 意为底部或地面，under 表示在其下。

items.en: Underground appears in the sixteenth century for things placed in the earth.
items.cn: underground 在十六世纪出现，指放在地里的东西。

items.en: The London railway takes the name in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪伦敦的铁路系统取用了这个名字。

items.en: The figurative sense of secret resistance grows in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 秘密抵抗的比喻义在十九、二十世纪成长起来。

items.en: American English prefers subway for the railway, keeping underground for the literal and secret senses.
items.cn: 美式英语用 subway 指地铁，underground 则保留字面义与秘密义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers under- compounds with ground, and the near-meaning group names underground things and hidden groups.
note.cn: 形近组汇集与 ground 相关的 under- 复合词，近义组列出地下与隐蔽的事物。

entries.definition: the surface of the earth
low plants under trees
what lies behind a thing
an underground railway, chiefly in America
a passage dug through earth
hidden from others
above the surface

normalIntro.en: Ground is the surface, and everything with under in front of it lies out of sight.
normalIntro.cn: ground 是地表，前面加了 under，就都到了看不见的地方。

normal.en: The British ride the underground and Americans ride the subway.
normal.cn: 英国人乘 the underground，美国人乘 subway。

normal.en: Go underground is the fixed phrase for going into hiding.
normal.cn: go underground 是「隐匿起来」的固定说法。

normal.en: Underground press and underground economy keep the secrecy sense.
normal.cn: underground press 与 underground economy 保留秘密义。

normal.en: Underground parking, underground cables, and underground rivers are all literal.
normal.cn: underground parking、cables、rivers 都是字面用法。

normal.en: The word stays the same in the plural, as a compound noun.
normal.cn: 复合名词下复数形式不变。

abstract.en: Go down a staircase that turns twice before the light returns.
abstract.cn: 沿一段拐两次弯才重见光的楼梯走下去。

abstract.en: Hear trains running under the streets you just left.
abstract.cn: 听见列车就在刚离开的街道下面运行。

abstract.en: Then picture a meeting held where no window can be found.
abstract.cn: 再想象在一处找不到窗子的地方开会。

examples.en: The cables run underground for most of the route.
examples.cn: 这条线路大部分的电缆埋在地下。

examples.en: Take the underground to the museum, it is faster.
examples.cn: 坐地铁去博物馆吧，更快。

examples.en: After the arrest he went underground for years.
examples.cn: 被捕之后，他转入地下好几年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安卓格朗德」——安卓机器人在地面之下（ground）钻洞跑地铁。

root: under（在下，古英语）+ ground（古英语 grund「底部、地面」）；英式名词指地铁，美式作 subway

sensesIntro.en: Every sense puts something below the surface: rails, cables, cars, newspapers, and whole movements.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都把某样东西放到地表以下：铁轨、电缆、车辆、报刊乃至整场运动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit tunnel running quietly under the soil.
core.cn: 核心意象：土层下安静延伸的亮灯隧道。

branches.en: The literal branch: car parks, cables, and rivers.
branches.cn: 字面分支：停车场、电缆与河流。

branches.en: The railway branch, a noun in British English.
branches.cn: 铁路分支：英式英语里的名词。

branches.en: The secrecy branch: press and economy outside the law.
branches.cn: 秘密分支：法律之外的地下报刊与经济。

branches.en: The hiding branch: a person who disappears.
branches.cn: 隐匿分支：消失不见的人。

branches.en: The plain sense used of anything buried.
branches.cn: 最普通的义项：任何埋于地下的东西。

intro.en: A preposition of position plus a noun for the surface of the earth.
intro.cn: 方位介词加一个表示地表的古英语名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source, so the Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 此词没有拉丁语来源，故拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.example: Grund means the earth below us.
items.exampleCN: grund 指我们脚下的大地。

definition_zh: 在…下画线；在…下面划线；强调；凸显
definition_en: to draw a line under a word or phrase, or to give special importance to something
core_image: 一支笔在纸上的字句下面压出一道笔直的横线，把这句话从纸面上抬起来
scene: 老师在黑板上写下一串生词，转身提醒全班把最难的那个词划出来。She underlined the word twice so nobody would miss it.
sceneCN: 这里 underline 是「在…下画线」（第 1 个义项：在文字下方画出线条）；句意为她把这个词划了两遍，好让谁都不会漏掉。纸上被划出的那道横线，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「下划线；划线做法」
由同义近形词构成，义为「在…下划线；强调」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「划线的；带下划线的」

senses.title: A line drawn beneath words
senses.definition: to draw a straight line under a word or phrase, usually to mark it as important
senses.definitionCN: 在词或短语下面画一条直线，通常用来标记其重要性
senses.example: She underlined every new word in her notebook.
senses.exampleCN: 她把笔记本里每个生词都划了下划线。
senses.why: The prefix under- puts the line below, and line is the stroke itself; the word is almost a picture of what it does.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 under- 把线放在下面，line 就是那道笔画；这个词几乎把动作画了出来。

senses.title: To stress a point
senses.definition: to give special emphasis to an idea, fact, or statement when speaking or writing
senses.definitionCN: 在说话或写作时特别强调某个想法、事实或说法
senses.example: The report underlines the need for cleaner water in the village.
senses.exampleCN: 报告强调了这个村子需要更干净的水。
senses.why: An underlined sentence is one the reader must not skip; stressing a point does the same thing with the voice.
senses.whyCN: 划线句是读者不能跳过的一句；强调某点就是用声音做同样的事。

senses.title: A mark of emphasis
senses.definition: a line drawn under written or printed words as a mark of emphasis or of a link
senses.definitionCN: 在书写或印刷文字下方画出的线，用作强调标记或链接标记
senses.example: The teacher put a red underline under the misspelled name.
senses.exampleCN: 老师在拼错的名字下面画了一道红色下划线。
senses.why: The verb became a noun: the stroke itself is now a thing you can see and point at.
senses.whyCN: 动词转成了名词：那道笔画本身成了看得见、指得出的东西。

senses.title: Printed with a line below
senses.definition: printed or displayed with a line beneath the letters, as links and titles often are
senses.definitionCN: 字母下方带有线条地印刷或显示，网页链接与标题常如此
senses.example: In the old dictionary every headword appears underlined in bold.
senses.exampleCN: 在那本旧词典里，每个词目都以加粗并划下划线的方式出现。
senses.why: Here the word describes the look of the text rather than an act: the line is already there.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词描述的是文字的样子而不是动作：线已经在那里了。

senses.title: To make something stand out
senses.definition: to make a quality, problem, or difference more obvious, as if drawing a line under it
senses.definitionCN: 使某种性质、问题或差别更加明显，如同在其下面画线
senses.example: The empty seats underlined how few people had come.
senses.exampleCN: 空着的座位更凸显出到场的人有多么少。
senses.why: The image moves off the page: whatever is underlined stands out from everything around it.
senses.whyCN: 意象离开了纸面：被划线的东西总是从周围一切中凸显出来。

intro.en: Underline is a plain English compound, made of a preposition and a Latin loanword, and it is recorded only from the modern period.
intro.cn: underline 是朴素的英语复合词，由一个介词与一个拉丁语借词组成，直到近代才有记录。

items.en: The preposition under is native Old English under, meaning beneath or below.
items.cn: 介词 under 是本土的古英语 under，意为「在……之下」。

items.en: The noun linea meant a linen thread used as a plumb line, and from it a drawn line.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 linea 原指铅垂用的麻线，后指画出的线。

items.en: Line entered English through Old French ligne, so the two halves of the compound come from different layers.
items.cn: line 经由古法语 ligne 进入英语，因此这个复合词的两半来自不同层次。

items.en: English joined under and line to name a stroke drawn beneath writing; the verb follows the noun closely.
items.cn: 英语把 under 与 line 合起来，指写在文字下方的一道笔画；动词紧随名词出现。

items.en: Later the word was extended to emphasis in speech and to anything that stands out from its background.
items.cn: 后来这个词被扩展到言语中的强调，以及任何从背景中凸显出来的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other words built with under-; the near-meaning group gathers marking and stressing verbs with different tools.
note.cn: 形近组收其他以 under- 构成的词；近义组收标记与强调的动词，所用手段各不相同。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning hidden beneath the surface but real and important.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「潜在的、根本的」，指藏在表面之下却真实重要。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning at a deeper or more basic level.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「从根本上、在更深层次上」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to weaken something gradually from below.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「逐渐削弱、从根基上破坏」。

entries.definition: A noun or verb for the outer edge or a summary; it looks close but means the opposite kind of line.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「轮廓、概要」；拼写相近，但指的是另一种线。

entries.definition: A noun for material laid under a carpet or floor covering.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「衬垫、地毯下面的垫层」。

entries.definition: To give special importance to something in speech or writing; it does not use a visible mark.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「强调」，用于言语或写作，不依赖可见的标记。

entries.definition: To mark text with colour or to draw attention to the most important part.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「用彩笔标出、突出」，多指用颜色而非线条。

entries.definition: To say a word or point with extra force, or to place emphasis on it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词「强调；重读」，指用更大的力气说出某词或某点。

entries.definition: To make a feature more noticeable; more formal and often about appearance.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使突出、加剧」，较正式，常指外观上的特征。

entries.definition: A general verb for putting a sign on something; underline is one particular kind of mark.
entries.definitionCN: 动词「标记」，泛指做记号；underline 是其中一种具体的标记方式。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two plain pieces of the compound and the situations where the word really appears.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个复合词的两个朴素部件，以及这个词真正出现的场合。

normal.en: under plus line: draw the line under the words.
normal.cn: under 加 line：把线画在字的下方。

normal.en: A teacher says underline it, and the class reaches for a ruler.
normal.cn: 老师说把这个词划出来，全班就去拿尺子。

normal.en: Highlight uses colour, underline uses a stroke.
normal.cn: highlight 用颜色，underline 用笔画。

normal.en: Underlined links are the old look of the web.
normal.cn: 带下划线的链接是网页早年常见的样子。

normal.en: A fact that underlines a problem makes it impossible to overlook.
normal.cn: underline 一个问题，就是让这个问题无法被忽略。

abstract.en: Think of a sheet of paper with one line pressed into it: everything above the line is what you must not miss.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸被压出一道线：线以上的内容就是你绝不能漏掉的部分。

abstract.en: The stroke can leave the paper: a silent empty hall underlines what nobody dared to say.
abstract.cn: 这道笔画可以离开纸面：空荡无声的大厅会强调谁也不敢说出口的话。

abstract.en: To underline is to choose: out of a whole page, one line is singled out to be seen.
abstract.cn: 划线就是选择：整页之中，只有一行被挑出来被看见。

examples.en: Please underline the words you do not know.
examples.cn: 请把你不认识的词划上横线。

examples.en: The mayor underlined that no new taxes would be raised this year.
examples.cn: 市长强调今年不会新增税收。

examples.en: Thin ice round the pond underlines the danger of skating there.
examples.cn: 池塘边薄薄的冰更凸显出在那里滑冰的危险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的莱恩」——安把莱恩的名字在纸下划了一道线：划下划线、强调

root: 由本土介词 under（古英语 under，在下面）与拉丁语 linea（麻线、线，经古法语 ligne 入英语）组成，字面即「在字下画线」，近代英语才合成此词。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of underline all keep one gesture: a stroke placed beneath something so that it stands apart from what surrounds it.
sensesIntro.cn: underline 的五个义项都保留同一个动作：在某物下方画一道笔画，让它从周围脱离出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pen draws a straight stroke right beneath a word on the page.
core.cn: 核心意象：笔在纸上的一个词下方画出笔直的一道线。

branches.en: THE PAGE: the hand draws the line under a word.
branches.cn: 纸面线：手在词的下方画出这条线。

branches.en: THE MARK: the stroke becomes a visible sign, and printed text can carry it already.
branches.cn: 标记线：笔画成为可见的标记，印刷文字也可以自带这道线。

branches.en: THE VOICE: stressing a point does with speech what the line does with ink.
branches.cn: 声音线：强调某点是用言语做这道线用墨水做的事。

branches.en: THE BACKGROUND: what is underlined stands out from everything around it.
branches.cn: 背景线：被划线之物从周围一切中凸显出来。

branches.en: THE GESTURE: from a school exercise to a warning sign, the same downward stroke is repeated.
branches.cn: 动作线：从课堂练习到警示信号，重复的都是同一道向下压的笔画。

intro.en: The compound is transparent: an English preposition plus a Latin noun, with ordinary suffixes for the rest of the family.
intro.cn: 这个复合词结构透明：一个英语介词加一个拉丁语名词，词族其余成员用普通后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin linea is recorded and came to English through Old French ligne; only the deeper root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 linea 有文献记录，经古法语 ligne 进入英语；只有更早的词根属于重构。

items.example: The prefix places the stroke lower than the letters.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把笔画放在字母的下方。

items.example: The noun names the stroke that gets drawn.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指被画出的那道笔画。

items.example: The Latin noun named the mason's cord.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词原指工匠用的麻绳。

items.example: French carried the noun into English.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个名词带进英语。

items.example: A close synonym built the same way.
items.exampleCN: 用同样方式构成的近义词。

items.example: The opposite kind of line, around rather than below.
items.exampleCN: 方向相反的另一种线：绕在外面而不是压在下边。

items.example: The word is its own best example.
items.exampleCN: 这个词本身就是自己最好的例子。

latinEntries.structure: Old French noun from Latin linea

definition_zh: 削弱；暗中破坏；逐渐损毁根基；动摇（信心、权威）
definition_en: to weaken something gradually from below, often secretly, by taking away what supports it
core_image: 老墙脚下，水从砖缝里一点点掏空泥沙，墙面看上去完好，根基却已经空了
scene: 老墙脚下，水从砖缝里一点点掏空泥沙，墙面看着完好，根基却已经空了。Constant leaks had begun to undermine the old wall.
sceneCN: 这里指从根基上逐渐削弱、掏空（第 1 个义项：损毁实物的基础）；句意为持续的渗漏已经开始逐渐损毁那面老墙。

pos.zh: 削弱；暗中破坏；逐渐损毁根基；动摇

derivatives.zh: 由该动词的现在分词转成的名词或形容词，义为「暗中破坏；起削弱作用的」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「暗中破坏者」
由该动词的过去分词转成的形容词，义为「已被削弱的；根基受损的」

senses.title: Hollow out a physical base
senses.definition: of water, digging or decay, to remove the material under a wall, road or building
senses.definitionCN: 指水、挖掘或腐朽移除墙、路或建筑底下的材料
senses.example: Salt water can undermine the foundation of a bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 盐水会逐渐掏空桥基。
senses.why: The word is literally under plus mine, so the first sense is the mining sense: taking the ground out from beneath a structure.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面上就是「在下」加「挖掘」，所以第一个义项就是采矿义：把结构底下的地基取走。

senses.title: Secretly damage a plan or effort
senses.definition: to weaken a plan, campaign or effort by quiet action rather than open opposition
senses.definitionCN: 以暗中行动而非公开反对来削弱计划、行动或努力
senses.example: A few leaks were enough to undermine the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 几次泄密就足以破坏那项计划。
senses.why: A tunnel dug under a defence does its work unseen, and the word kept that secrecy when it moved from walls to plans.
senses.whyCN: 在防线底下挖的坑道在看不见处做工，这个词从墙转到计划时保留了那份隐秘。

senses.title: Weaken a person's confidence
senses.definition: to make someone steadily less sure of themselves or of a decision
senses.definitionCN: 使某人对自己或某个决定逐渐失去把握
senses.example: Constant criticism undermined her confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 不断的批评削弱了她的信心。
senses.why: Confidence stands on supports, and enough small attacks from below can make it sag without ever being hit directly.
senses.whyCN: 信心立在支撑上，足够多来自下方的小攻击能让它下沉，却从未被直接击中。

senses.title: Shake an authority or position
senses.definition: to make a leader, office or institution less respected and less able to act
senses.definitionCN: 使领导者、职位或机构受到的尊重减少、行动能力下降
senses.example: The scandal undermined the minister's authority.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻动摇了那位部长的权威。
senses.why: Authority is a structure that stands on accepted ground, and removing that ground is the word's exact work.
senses.whyCN: 权威是立在公认地基上的结构，而抽走那层地基正是这个词的确切工作。

senses.title: Damage a reputation
senses.definition: to lower the trust that others place in a person, company or brand
senses.definitionCN: 降低他人对个人、公司或品牌的信任
senses.example: Rumours undermined the company's reputation.
senses.exampleCN: 谣言损害了公司的声誉。
senses.why: A reputation is built from many small confirmations, so it can be undone from below without any single open attack.
senses.whyCN: 声誉由许多小确认堆成，因此可以被下方一点点拆掉，而无需任何一次公开攻击。

senses.title: Weaken an argument
senses.definition: to make a case less convincing by removing the support under one of its claims
senses.definitionCN: 抽掉某个主张底下的支撑，使论证不那么令人信服
senses.example: One weak example undermined the whole argument.
senses.exampleCN: 一个薄弱的例证削弱了整个论证。
senses.why: An argument is a building of reasons, and the word is used for taking a load-bearing stone out of it.
senses.whyCN: 论证是由理由搭起的建筑，这个词就用来形容从中抽走一块承重的石头。

senses.title: Dig beneath a seam or deposit
senses.definition: in mining, to cut a tunnel under a body of coal or ore so that it can be removed
senses.definitionCN: 采矿中指在煤层或矿体下方开掘巷道以便采出
senses.example: Miners undermined the seam from a lower tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工从下方的巷道掏挖那层煤层。
senses.why: This is the technical sense that keeps the two halves of the word visible: under, and mine.
senses.whyCN: 这是让词的两个半截都保持可见的技术义：在下，以及挖掘。

senses.title: Sap physical strength
senses.definition: of illness, hunger or overwork, to wear down a person's strength slowly
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病、饥饿或过劳缓慢损耗一个人的体力
senses.example: Illness had undermined his strength over the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 疾病在冬天里一点点损耗了他的体力。
senses.why: The body also has foundations, and slow removal from below describes a decline that no single event explains.
senses.whyCN: 身体也有根基，而从下方缓慢抽走，描述的是一种无法归因于单一事件的衰退。

senses.title: Break the ground under trust
senses.definition: to make the trust between people or groups collapse through repeated small betrayals
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复的小背叛使人或群体之间的信任崩塌
senses.example: Broken promises undermined the trust between them.
senses.exampleCN: 屡次食言破坏了他们之间的信任。
senses.why: Trust rests on a floor of kept promises, and this word describes the floor being taken away one tile at a time.
senses.whyCN: 信任铺在守诺的地板上，而这个词描述的就是地板被一块块抽走。

intro.en: Undermine is an English compound of under and mine. The first half is native Old English; the second came through Old French and its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语由「在下」与「矿、挖掘」构成的复合词。前半是本土古英语，后半经古法语而来，其更深来源不明。

items.en: Under is a native preposition and prefix meaning below, and it has shaped hundreds of English compounds.
items.cn: under 是本土介词与副词，意为在下方，它参与构成了数以百计的英语复合词。

items.en: The noun meant a mine, an ore bed or a subterranean passage, and English borrowed it in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 这个名词意为矿、矿层或地下通道，英语在中世纪借入。

items.en: The written source is mina, but its own origin is uncertain; it may have come from a Celtic word for ore.
items.cn: 有记载的来源是 mina，但它自身的来源不明，可能来自某支凯尔特语中表示矿石的词。

items.en: The verb first meant to dig under a wall or a fort so that it would fall; the military sense is the oldest recorded one.
items.cn: 这个动词最初意为在墙或堡垒底下挖掘使之倒塌；军事义是最早有记载的义项。

items.en: From digging under defences the word moved to weakening confidence, authority and trust; the date of each shift is uncertain.
items.cn: 从在防线底下挖掘，这个词转向削弱信心、权威与信任；每次转变的年代不确定。

items.en: Medicine uses it for slow declines of strength and immunity that no single cause can explain.
items.cn: 医学用它形容无法归因于单一原因的体力与免疫力缓慢衰退。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like undermine; the second group names neighbouring ways of weakening something.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 undermine 相近；第二组是与「削弱、破坏」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The act of weakening something from below or in secret.
entries.definitionCN: 指从下方或暗中削弱某物的行为。

entries.definition: A person who quietly damages a plan or an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 指暗中破坏计划或权威的人。

entries.definition: An excavation for ore, or the act of digging one; the second half of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 指矿坑，或挖掘矿坑的行为；是本词的后半部分。

entries.definition: Below the surface of the earth; it shares the prefix but not the mining verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指地面之下；共享前缀，但不含那个挖掘动词。

entries.definition: To take on a task; it shares the prefix but has an unrelated second half.
entries.definitionCN: 指承担任务；共享前缀，但后半部分无关。

entries.definition: To make less strong; the broad word, with no image of digging or secrecy.
entries.definitionCN: 指使变弱；最宽泛的词，不含挖掘或隐秘的意象。

entries.definition: To wear something away gradually by wind, water or friction; it stresses slow surface loss.
entries.definitionCN: 指风、水或摩擦逐渐磨损；强调表面的缓慢流失。

entries.definition: To damage something deliberately, usually from inside an organisation; it stresses intent.
entries.definitionCN: 指故意破坏，通常从组织内部下手；强调意图。

entries.definition: To overturn an authority or system from within; it stresses turning the order upside down.
entries.definitionCN: 指从内部颠覆权威或制度；强调把秩序翻过来。

entries.definition: To reduce the function of something; it stresses loss of working ability rather than support.
entries.definitionCN: 指降低某物的功能；强调工作能力的损失，而非支撑。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two visible halves, under and mine, and the image of ground removed from beneath.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想利用两个看得见的半截——「在下」与「挖掘」，以及从底下抽走地面的意象。

normal.en: Say the two halves in order: under, then mine. The word is a tunnel dug beneath a wall.
normal.cn: 按顺序念两个半截：先「在下」，再「挖掘」。这个词就是在墙底下挖的一条坑道。

normal.en: A wall can look perfect from the street while the ground beneath it has already been taken away.
normal.cn: 一面墙从街上看似完好，它底下的土却早已被掏走。

normal.en: A rumour works like water in a brick joint: no hammer, but the joint gets wider.
normal.cn: 谣言像砖缝里的水：没有锤子，缝却越来越宽。

normal.en: The word is always gradual; it never means one clean blow.
normal.cn: 这个词总是渐进的，从不指干净利落的一击。

normal.en: The secret is part of the meaning: the damage is done where no one is looking.
normal.cn: 隐秘是意义的一部分：破坏发生在没人看的地方。

abstract.en: Undermining is the quiet form of opposition, and it is harder to answer than an open attack.
abstract.cn: 暗中破坏是反对的安静形式，比公开攻击更难回应。

abstract.en: Structures fail from below long before they fail from the front.
abstract.cn: 结构从下方失效，远早于它从正面失效。

abstract.en: What is undermined is not destroyed but left standing on nothing.
abstract.cn: 被掏空的东西不是被摧毁，而是被留在虚无之上继续立着。

examples.en: The constant flooding undermined the road's foundations.
examples.cn: 反复的洪水损毁了那条路的地基。

examples.en: His careless remarks undermined the peace talks.
examples.cn: 他轻率的言论破坏了和谈。

examples.en: Low pay undermines the morale of the whole team.
examples.cn: 低薪削弱了整个团队的士气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「安德曼」——「安德」是「在下」，在墙「曼」慢地挖，墙就从底下空了：暗中削弱

root: 古英语 under「在下」+ 古法语 mine「矿、挖掘」→ 中古英语 undermine「在墙下挖坑道使之倒塌」→ 现代义「从根基上逐渐削弱、暗中破坏」；其中「矿」的更深来源不明，可能出自凯尔特语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses keep one direction, from below and often unseen: a foundation, a plan, a confidence, an authority, a reputation, an argument, a coal seam, a body and the trust between people.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项保持同一个方向——自下而上、常在暗处：地基、计划、信心、权威、声誉、论证、煤层、身体，以及人与人之间的信任。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water taking sand out of a brick joint until the wall stands on emptiness.
core.cn: 核心意象：水把砖缝里的沙一点点带走，直到墙立在空处。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL BASE BRANCH: water takes a bridge's foundation, and miners cut under a seam.
branches.cn: 实物根基分支：水掏空桥基，矿工在煤层下方开挖。

branches.en: THE PLAN AND ARGUMENT BRANCH: leaks damage a campaign and one weak example damages a case.
branches.cn: 计划与论证分支：泄密破坏行动，一个薄弱例证破坏论证。

branches.en: THE INNER STRENGTH BRANCH: criticism lowers confidence and illness lowers bodily strength.
branches.cn: 内在力量分支：批评压低信心，疾病损耗体力。

branches.en: THE AUTHORITY BRANCH: a scandal removes the ground a minister stands on.
branches.cn: 权威分支：丑闻抽走部长脚下的地基。

branches.en: THE REPUTATION AND TRUST BRANCH: rumours spoil a name and broken promises spoil a bond.
branches.cn: 声誉与信任分支：谣言毁掉名声，食言毁掉纽带。

intro.en: Undermine is a native prefix on a borrowed noun, and the join is so old that English speakers no longer feel the two parts separately.
intro.cn: 这是一个本土前缀加在借来的名词上，接合得太久，英语使用者已不再分别感觉这两个部分。

latinIntro.en: The second half reached English through Old French from Medieval Latin mina, a word of uncertain origin that may be Celtic.
latinIntro.cn: 后半部分经古法语、来自中世纪拉丁语 mina，这个词来源不明，可能出自凯尔特语。

items.example: It fixes the direction of the damage from the start.
items.exampleCN: 它从一开始就定下破坏的方向。

items.meaning: a pit for ore, a subterranean passage
items.example: The noun supplies the digging that the verb describes.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供动词所描述的挖掘动作。

items.structure: English verb converted from the noun
items.example: English turned the pit into an action without adding an ending.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个坑直接变成动作，没有加词尾。

items.example: It forms the noun for the slow work of weakening.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「缓慢削弱」这一工作的名词。

items.example: It names the person who digs from below.
items.exampleCN: 它命名从下方挖掘的人。

items.example: It forms undermined, a position already weakened.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 undermined，表示已被削弱的处境。

items.meaning: the act of weakening from below
items.meaningCN: 从下方逐渐削弱的行为
items.example: The constant undermining of trust ruined the talks.
items.exampleCN: 对信任的持续侵蚀毁了会谈。

items.meaning: one who digs from below or weakens in secret
items.meaningCN: 从下方挖掘或暗中削弱的人
items.example: An underminer works out of sight.
items.exampleCN: 暗中破坏者在看不见的地方行事。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词的现在分词转成的名词或形容词，义为「暗中破坏；起削弱作用的」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「暗中破坏者」
由该动词的过去分词转成的形容词，义为「已被削弱的；根基受损的」

definition_zh: 在……下面；在底下；隐蔽地；（作名词）底部
definition_en: directly under something, often so as to be hidden by it
core_image: 掀开毯子一角，底下那层东西严严实实地藏着
scene: 搬家时，老沙发被抬起，底下卷着的一枚硬币和一张旧照片滚了出来。The letter was hidden underneath a stack of newspapers.
sceneCN: 这里 underneath 是「在……下面」（第 1 个义项：正下方、被遮住）；句意为那封信藏在一摞报纸下面。掀开毯角看见底下藏的那层，正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 同源介词，义为「在……下面」
近义介词，义为「在……下方」
复合名词，义为「底面」

senses.title: Directly under and covered by
senses.definition: placed just under something that hides it
senses.definitionCN: 就在某物之下，被它遮住
senses.example: The cat is asleep underneath the chair.
senses.exampleCN: 猫在椅子底下睡着。
senses.why: Under is the old preposition and nīthe added a sense of below from beneath, giving a more pointed down there.
senses.whyCN: under 是古老介词，nīthe 带出 beneath 意味，合起来更强调「就在下方那一层」。

senses.title: Hidden beneath a surface
senses.definition: concealed below what shows
senses.definitionCN: 藏在外观所见之物的下面
senses.example: There is a layer of clay underneath the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 土层底下有一层黏土。
senses.why: A surface only reports its top, so whatever lies in the next layer counts as concealed.
senses.whyCN: 表面只会报出它最上面一层，所以落在下一层里的东西都算被藏住。

senses.title: Used alone for the lower side
senses.definition: used alone to mean on the underside or in the inner part
senses.definitionCN: 单独使用，指在底面或内里
senses.example: The plate is gold underneath.
senses.exampleCN: 这只盘子底下是金的。
senses.why: The adverb lets the speaker point downward without naming the object.
senses.whyCN: 副词让说话人不点出对象，只把手指往下一指。

senses.title: Beneath a surface appearance
senses.definition: below the outward manner, of feelings not displayed
senses.definitionCN: 指外表之下的情绪，未必显现出来
senses.example: Underneath he was more pleased than he showed.
senses.exampleCN: 内里他比他表现出来的更高兴。
senses.why: The physical layer beneath becomes the emotional layer beneath.
senses.whyCN: 实物的那一层之下，转成情绪的那一层之下。

senses.title: The underside of a thing
senses.definition: the lower surface of an object
senses.definitionCN: 物体的下表面
senses.example: The underneath of the boat was covered in weed.
senses.exampleCN: 船底长满了水草。
senses.why: The adverb turns into a noun by naming the lower face itself.
senses.whyCN: 副词一旦直接称呼那个下表面，就成了名词。

intro.en: The word joins under with an Old English word for below.
intro.cn: 这个词把 under 与一个古英语的「在下」词根接在一起。

items.en: Under is the inherited preposition, and neothan or nithan means from below.
items.cn: under 是固有介词，nēothan 或 nithan 意为「从下面」。

items.en: Underneothan combines both and is recorded in Old English.
items.cn: underneothan 把两者合起来，古英语已有记录。

items.en: Middle English shortens the form toward underneath as it is spelled today.
items.cn: 中古英语把形式缩短为今天的 underneath。

items.en: The figurative use for hidden feelings settles in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 指隐藏情绪的比喻用法在十九世纪定型。

items.en: The noun use for an underside is chiefly informal.
items.cn: 指底面的名词用法主要属非正式语体。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers prepositions ending in a downward element, and the near-meaning group gathers words of lower position.
note.cn: 形近组汇集带「在下」部件的介词，近义组汇集表示低处之词。

entries.definition: below
directly under
below the surface
at a lower level
the lower face of a thing
above
the lowest supporting part

normalIntro.en: Under plus an old word for below makes the most pointed of all the down words.
normalIntro.cn: under 加一个古语「在下」词，成了所有「下方」词里最实指的一个。

normal.en: Think of underneath as the exact layer hidden by the thing above.
normal.cn: 把 underneath 想成被上面那件东西遮住的那一层。

normal.en: Beneath and underneath are nearly the same, but underneath usually touches.
normal.cn: beneath 与 underneath 几乎一样，但 underneath 通常紧贴。

normal.en: Underneath as an adverb can stand after the verb, as in gold underneath.
normal.cn: underneath 作副词时能放在动词后，如 gold underneath。

normal.en: The noun use, the underneath, means the underside of a thing.
normal.cn: 名词用法 the underneath 指物体的底面。

normal.en: Underneath the surface and underneath it all are the two figurative phrases.
normal.cn: underneath the surface 与 underneath it all 是两个比喻性搭配。

abstract.en: Lift one corner of a blanket and see what stayed hidden.
abstract.cn: 掀开毯子一角，看见一直藏着的东西。

abstract.en: Notice the layer is not far away, only covered.
abstract.cn: 注意那一层并不远，只是被盖住了。

abstract.en: Then let a calm face cover a glad feeling the same way.
abstract.cn: 再让一张平静的脸以同样方式盖住喜悦。

examples.en: The dog sleeps underneath the old kitchen table.
examples.cn: 那条狗睡在旧厨房桌子底下。

examples.en: Underneath all the noise, she was a kind person.
examples.cn: 在所有的喧闹之下，她是个善良的人。

examples.en: The underneath of the shelf was still sticky with paint.
examples.cn: 架子底面还粘着油漆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺的尼思」——俺的思绪藏在最底下一层，谁都看不见。

root: under（古英语介词）+ nēothan／nithan（从下面），合为古英语 underneothan，中古英语缩短为 underneath

sensesIntro.en: The word points to the exact layer covered by something: a cat, a coin, a clay bed, or a feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词指向被某物盖住的那一层：一只猫、一枚硬币、一层黏土，或一种心情。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a corner of a blanket lifted to show what was under it.
core.cn: 核心意象：掀开毯角，露出底下藏着的东西。

branches.en: The place branch: cats, tables, and chairs.
branches.cn: 位置分支：猫、桌子与椅子。

branches.en: The layer branch: clay, coins, old letters.
branches.cn: 层叠分支：黏土、硬币与旧信。

branches.en: The adverb branch, where no object is named.
branches.cn: 副词分支：不点出对象。

branches.en: The feeling branch: what a calm surface hides.
branches.cn: 情绪分支：平静表面所藏。

branches.en: The noun branch: the underside of a boat.
branches.cn: 名词分支：船底。

intro.en: Two inherited words for below stacked into one.
intro.cn: 两个表示「在下」的固有词叠成一个。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source, so the Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 此词没有拉丁语来源，故拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.exampleCN: nēothan 增添了「下方」的强调。

items.example: A key lay underneath the mat.
items.exampleCN: 垫子底下放着一把钥匙。

items.example: Beneath the tree stood a bench.

definition_zh: 理解；懂得；了解；体谅；认为；听说
definition_en: to know what something means or how it works, or to know another’s feelings
core_image: 站在对方的立场上，忽然看清了他说那句话时的处境
scene: 老师把学生的作业本翻过来，看到他昨天晚上在页边写的一行小字，语气软了下来。Now I understand why she left so early.
sceneCN: 这里 understand 是「理解、明白」（第 1 个义项：懂得含义或缘由）；句意为现在我明白她为什么这么早走了。站到对方位置上看清他的处境，正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -ing 构成名词，义为「理解；谅解」
动词加 -able 构成形容词，义为「可以理解的」
加前缀 mis- 构成动词，义为「误解」

senses.title: To grasp the meaning of something
senses.definition: to know what words, rules, or ideas mean
senses.definitionCN: 知道文字、规则或想法的意思
senses.example: Do you understand the question?
senses.exampleCN: 你明白这个问题吗？
senses.why: The old verb stand means to be in place, so to understand is to stand in the place of a thing and see it from there.
senses.whyCN: 古语 stand 意为站立，understand 就是站到一件事的立场上去看它。

senses.title: To see the reason behind something
senses.definition: to know why something happened or was said
senses.definitionCN: 知道某事为何发生或被说出
senses.example: I understand now why he refused.
senses.exampleCN: 我现在明白他为什么拒绝了。
senses.why: Grasping a fact and grasping its reason are one act of standing in its place.
senses.whyCN: 抓住一个事实与抓住它的缘由，是同一个「站到它位置上」的动作。

senses.title: To know another person’s feelings
senses.definition: to be aware of and accept how someone feels
senses.definitionCN: 察觉并接受某人的感受
senses.example: My parents do not always understand me.
senses.exampleCN: 父母并不总能理解我。
senses.why: When you stand where another stands, feeling comes before facts.
senses.whyCN: 站到别人的位置上，感受先于事实到来。

senses.title: To believe or be told
senses.definition: to have been informed that something is so
senses.definitionCN: 据告知而认为某事如此
senses.example: I understand that the meeting has been moved.
senses.exampleCN: 我听说会议改期了。
senses.why: What you have taken in as true is also what you stand under as information.
senses.whyCN: 你当作真的收进来的消息，也是你站在其下接受的信息。

senses.title: To supply a missing word mentally
senses.definition: to take a word as implied though it is not written
senses.definitionCN: 把未写出的词含在心里补上
senses.example: In this phrase the verb is understood.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个短语里那个动词是隐含的。
senses.why: The reader joins the writer by standing in the same place and filling the gap.
senses.whyCN: 读者站到作者的同一位置，把空缺补上，两端就此接合。

intro.en: The word is an Old English compound of standing under something.
intro.cn: 这个词是古英语复合词，意为站在某物之下。

items.en: Understandan is built from under and standan, to stand, and means to stand in the midst of.
items.cn: understandan 由 under 与 standan（站立）构成，意为「站在其中」。

items.en: The prefix here is close in force to inter, so the word means to be among a thing.
items.cn: 这里的前缀效力接近 inter，因此这个词意为「处于某物之中」。

items.en: Middle English understand has already narrowed toward knowing and comprehending.
items.cn: 中古英语中 understand 已经收窄到「知晓、领会」。

items.en: The past forms understood, both past and participle, are leveled in the modern period.
items.cn: 过去式与过去分词在现代统一为 understood。

items.en: The polite sense of believing what one is told is common in business letters.
items.cn: 表示「据闻」的客气义在商务信函里很常见。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs built on stand, and the near-meaning group collects verbs of grasping meaning.
note.cn: 形近组汇集由 stand 构成的动词，近义组汇集表示领会意义的动词。

entries.definition: the ability to grasp and to be kind
to grasp something wrongly
to stand against and resist
to grasp fully
to seize mentally
