to take the wrong meaning

normalIntro.en: Stand under a thing and look up at it from there, and you know how it stands.
normalIntro.cn: 站到一件事的下面抬头去看，就知道它到底是怎么立的。

normal.en: Understand and withstand share the verb stand, one standing among, one standing against.
normal.cn: understand 与 withstand 共用 stand，一个是站在其中，一个是顶住。

normal.en: Comprehend and grasp both picture taking hold, while understand pictures taking a place.
normal.cn: comprehend 与 grasp 都像伸手抓住，understand 则像占住一个位置。

normal.en: Understanding is the noun and also means a friendly tolerance between people.
normal.cn: understanding 既是名词「理解」，也指人与人之间的体谅。

normal.en: Misunderstand adds mis- for a wrong stand, a look from the wrong place.
normal.cn: misunderstand 加 mis-，表示站错了位置、从错处去看。

normal.en: Understood serves as both past tense and past participle.
normal.cn: understood 同时充当过去式与过去分词。

abstract.en: Step into another person’s shoes without saying a word.
abstract.cn: 不说一句话，把脚伸进别人的鞋里。

abstract.en: Look back at your own remark from there and feel it change.
abstract.cn: 从那儿回头看自己那句话，会觉得它变了样。

abstract.en: Then put a missing word into a gap and watch the sentence close.
abstract.cn: 再往空缺里填一个词，看句子合上。

examples.en: I did not understand the instructions at first.
examples.cn: 一开始我没看懂这些说明。

examples.en: She understands how hard the decision was for you.
examples.cn: 她明白这个决定对你有多难。

examples.en: We understand that the office will close early today.
examples.cn: 我们听说办公室今天会提前关门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的斯坦得」——安心地站在（stand）对方那边，自然就懂了。

root: 古英语 under（在其下／在其中）+ standan（站立），understandan 意为「站在其中」，过去式与过去分词均为 understood

sensesIntro.en: Each sense is a change of place: standing in a thing, in a reason, in a feeling, in a report, or in a gap.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都是一次换位：站进一件事、一个缘由、一种感受、一则传闻，或一处空缺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: standing where another stands and seeing what they see.
core.cn: 核心意象：站到别人站的地方，看见他所看见的。

branches.en: The language branch: meanings and implied words.
branches.cn: 语言分支：意义与隐含的词。

branches.en: The cause branch: why a thing happened.
branches.cn: 原因分支：事情为何发生。

branches.en: The people branch: standing inside another’s feeling.
branches.cn: 人分支：站进别人的感受里。

branches.en: The report branch: what one has taken in as true.
branches.cn: 传闻分支：被当作真而收进来的话。

branches.en: The plain classroom sense of getting the point.
branches.cn: 课堂里最普通的「听懂了」。

intro.en: Two native English pieces: a preposition of place and a verb of standing.
intro.cn: 两块土生英语部件：一个方位介词和一个站立的动词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source, so the Latin list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 此词没有拉丁语来源，故拉丁同源词一栏留空。

items.example: Under here means in the midst of.
items.exampleCN: 这里的 under 意为「处于其中」。

definition_zh: 承担；着手做；从事；承诺；保证
definition_en: to accept a task or responsibility and begin to carry it out, or to promise formally that you will do something
core_image: 一个人蹲下身，把倒在地上的重物扛到自己肩上，然后站起来往前走
scene: 工程队接到山区修路的委托，队长在会议室里沉默地看了很久地图。He agreed to undertake the work before the rainy season.
sceneCN: 这里 undertake 是「承担某项工作」（第 1 个义项：接受任务并开始去做）；句意为他在雨季到来之前答应承担这项工程。把重物扛上肩的那个动作，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「任务；事业；承诺」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「承办人；殡葬承办者」
由过去分词转用，义为「已承担的；被承办的」

senses.title: Take a task onto yourself
senses.definition: to accept a piece of work or a duty and start doing it
senses.definitionCN: 接受一项工作或职责并开始去做
senses.example: The firm agreed to undertake the repairs at its own cost.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司同意自费承担维修工作。
senses.why: Under- is beneath and take is to grasp: you take the load onto yourself and carry it from below.
senses.whyCN: under- 是「在下」，take 是「抓住」：你把重负抓过来搁在自己身上，从下面托着走。

senses.title: Promise to do it
senses.definition: to promise, often in a formal way, that you will do something
senses.definitionCN: 通常以正式方式承诺自己会做某事
senses.example: Both sides undertook to keep the talks secret.
senses.exampleCN: 双方承诺对会谈内容保密。
senses.why: Once a task is taken on, the promise is simply the spoken side of the same act.
senses.whyCN: 任务一旦承担下来，承诺就是这同一个动作说出来的那一面。

senses.title: Carry out a study or inquiry
senses.definition: to begin and carry through an organized activity such as a study, survey, or repair
senses.definitionCN: 开始并完成研究、调查、维修等有组织的活动
senses.example: The team will undertake a full survey of the river next spring.
senses.exampleCN: 团队明年春天将对这条河进行全面调查。
senses.why: Research is heavy work that someone must lift; it is undertaken the way a load is.
senses.whyCN: 研究是一件必须由人抬起的重活，承担它的方式就像扛起一包货物。

senses.title: Formally agree to be responsible
senses.definition: to agree formally to be responsible for a job, especially for payment or delivery
senses.definitionCN: 正式同意对某项工作负责，尤指付款或交付
senses.example: A local builder undertook to finish the bridge by October.
senses.exampleCN: 一家本地建筑商承办了在十月前建成这座桥的任务。
senses.why: This is the legal face of the load: the contract states who has agreed to carry it.
senses.whyCN: 这是重负在法律上的样子：合同写明由谁同意去扛。

senses.title: Set out on a journey
senses.definition: to start on a long journey or a difficult course of action
senses.definitionCN: 开始一段长途旅行或一条艰难的行动路线
senses.example: They undertook the crossing in small boats at night.
senses.exampleCN: 他们夜里乘小船完成了这次横渡。
senses.why: A journey is taken up like a load: you commit your body to it before you know the end.
senses.whyCN: 旅程像货物一样被扛起：在知道结局之前，你就先把身体交付出去。

intro.en: Undertake is a native English compound of under and take, whose sense shifted from catching hold from below to taking a duty on oneself.
intro.cn: undertake 是英语本土复合词，由 under 与 take 组成，词义由「从下面接住」转为「把责任担到自己身上」。

items.en: Take comes from Old Norse taka, to grasp or seize, which replaced the Old English verb niman.
items.cn: take 来自古诺尔斯语 taka（抓取、拿），它取代了古英语动词 niman。

items.en: The compound first meant to intercept or catch hold of something, especially from below.
items.cn: 这个复合词最初意为拦截或接住某物，尤其指从下方托住。

items.en: From taking hold of a task came the sense of taking it upon oneself as a duty.
items.cn: 由「抓住一项任务」生出「把它作为职责担在自己身上」的意思。

items.en: The formal promise sense settled in, and undertake to do became common in contracts and letters.
items.cn: 正式的承诺义稳定下来，undertake to do 成为合同与书信中的常见说法。

items.en: Today the word covers research, repairs, journeys and any duty a person agrees to carry.
items.cn: 今天这个词涵盖研究、维修、旅程以及任何一个人同意承担的义务。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other compounds in under- and the formally similar mistake word; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of assuming duties with different strength.
note.cn: 形近组收其他以 under- 构成的复合词以及形似的易混词；近义组收表示承担职责的动词，力度各不相同。

entries.definition: A person who arranges funerals; it is formed from undertake plus -er.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「殡葬承办人」，由 undertake 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: A task or a formal promise; the noun form of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「任务、承诺」，是本词的名词形式。

entries.definition: To pass another vehicle or to catch up with someone; the prefix is over, not under.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「超车、赶上」，前缀是 over 而不是 under。

entries.definition: The irregular past tense, used for a duty taken on in the past.
entries.definitionCN: 不规则过去式，用于过去承担的职责。

entries.definition: An error, or to confuse one thing with another; it shares the take ending only.
entries.definitionCN: 名词「错误」或动词「弄错」，只与 take 这一部分相同。

entries.definition: To take on a duty or role, often without being asked; more silent than undertake.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承担、就任」，常指未被要求便接下，比 undertake 更少声张。

entries.definition: The everyday phrasal verb for accepting work or responsibility.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语，义为「承担、接受工作或责任」，最为口语。

entries.definition: To promise time, money, or effort to something; stresses locking oneself in.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「投入、承诺」，强调把自己锁定在某事上。

entries.definition: To begin something new and large, especially a project or journey.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语，义为「着手、开始」，多指宏大而新的事业或旅程。

entries.definition: A general verb for agreeing to receive or do something; it lacks the image of carrying.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「接受」，属一般用语，不含「扛起」的意象。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the literal pieces of the compound and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个复合词的各个部件，以及这个词真正出现的搭配。

normal.en: Under plus take: take the job up from underneath and hold it.
normal.cn: under 加 take：从下面把活儿托起来抓住。

normal.en: A team undertakes a survey; a builder undertakes the repairs.
normal.cn: 团队承担调查；建筑商承办维修。

normal.en: Undertake to do something is a formal promise, as in a contract.
normal.cn: undertake to do something 是正式承诺，常见于合同。

normal.en: The past form is undertook, the participle is undertaken.
normal.cn: 过去式是 undertook，过去分词是 undertaken。

normal.en: An undertaker takes on the last duty for a family.
normal.cn: undertaker 是替一个家庭承担最后那件事的人。

abstract.en: Picture a load that has no handles: to move it you must get underneath, and that is exactly what the word says.
abstract.cn: 想象一包没有提手的东西：要搬动它你必须钻到底下，而这正是这个词说的动作。

abstract.en: Every obligation is weight: undertake measures how much of it you agree to lift.
abstract.cn: 每项义务都有重量：undertake 衡量的是你同意抬起多少。

abstract.en: The word joins promise and effort, so saying it commits both the voice and the hands.
abstract.cn: 这个词把承诺与力气系在一起，说出口就等于同时交出了声音和双手。

examples.en: She undertook the difficult task of rebuilding the school library.
examples.cn: 她承担了重建学校图书馆这项艰难任务。

examples.en: The company has undertaken to reduce its waste by half.
examples.cn: 公司已承诺把废弃物减少一半。

examples.en: Two students undertook a study of traffic near the school gate.
examples.cn: 两名学生对学校门口的交通状况开展了研究。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的退克」——安退一步，把重活扛上肩：承担、承诺

root: 由 under（古英语 under，在下）与 take（古诺尔斯语 taka，抓取）合成；早期义为「从下面承接、拦截」，中古英语起转为「把任务担在自己身上」，近代定型为承担与正式承诺。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of undertake all describe one movement: getting beneath a weight and agreeing to carry it, whether it is work, a promise, a study, a contract, or a journey.
sensesIntro.cn: undertake 的五个义项都描述同一个动作：钻到重物下方并同意去扛它，无论那是工作、承诺、研究、合同还是旅程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone crouches, slides under a heavy load, and stands up carrying it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人蹲下，钻到重物底下，然后扛着它站起来。

branches.en: THE WORK: a task is accepted and carried from the first day.
branches.cn: 工作线：任务被接受，并从第一天起就扛着走。

branches.en: THE WORD GIVEN: the same load is promised out loud.
branches.cn: 言辞线：同一份重负被说出口地承诺下来。

branches.en: THE STUDY: research and surveys are long loads that must be lifted first.
branches.cn: 研究线：研究与调查是需要先抬起来的长途重负。

branches.en: THE CONTRACT: in law the word records who has agreed to carry what.
branches.cn: 合同线：在法律上这个词记录谁同意扛什么。

branches.en: THE JOURNEY: a long road is taken up as a load is taken up.
branches.cn: 旅程线：漫长的路像重物一样被扛起。

intro.en: Undertake is built from a native prefix and a borrowed Norse verb, and the noun family grows with English suffixes.
intro.cn: undertake 由一个本土前缀与一个借自诺尔斯语的动词构成，名词家族由英语后缀生长出来。

latinIntro.en: Neither piece is Latin: under is native and taka is Old Norse, so the Latin table here records only later scholarly relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都不是拉丁语：under 是本土词，taka 是古诺尔斯语；此处的拉丁条目只记录后世的学术同源词。

items.example: The prefix shows the load being lifted from below.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀表示重物是从下面被抬起的。

items.example: The verb names the grip on the task.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指对任务的抓握。

items.example: Norse settlers brought the verb into English.
items.exampleCN: 诺尔斯移民把这个动词带入英语。

items.example: The older native verb was pushed out by taka.
items.exampleCN: 更早的本土动词被 taka 取代。

items.example: The irregular past keeps the old vowel pattern.
items.exampleCN: 不规则过去式保留了古老的元音变化。

items.meaning: one who takes on a task
items.example: Its modern sense shifted to funerals only.
items.exampleCN: 其现代义已缩窄到殡葬承办。

definition_zh: 水下的；在水中的；水下使用的
definition_en: lying, happening, or used below the surface of the sea, a lake, or a river
core_image: 一个人把头埋进清亮的水面以下，看见阳光在头顶碎成一片晃动的光斑
scene: 潜摄小组清晨出发，海面平静得像一块玻璃。An underwater camera filmed the coral reef for two hours.
sceneCN: 这里 underwater 是「水下的」（第 1 个义项：位于水面以下）；句意为一台水下摄像机把珊瑚礁拍了两小时。沉到水面以下的那个世界，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 水下；水中部分（少见用法）

derivatives.zh: 由同义近形词构成，义为「海底的」
由拉丁语 sub-「在下」加 mergere「浸入」构成，义为「被水淹没的」

senses.title: Below the surface
senses.definition: situated or happening below the surface of a body of water
senses.definitionCN: 位于或发生在水体表面以下
senses.example: The divers spent an hour underwater looking for the wreck.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水员在水下待了一小时寻找那艘沉船。
senses.why: Under is beneath and water is water: the word simply puts one thing below the other.
senses.whyCN: under 是「在下面」，water 是「水」：这个词就是把一样东西放到另一样下面。

senses.title: Made for use down there
senses.definition: designed, built, or used for working below the surface
senses.definitionCN: 为在水面以下工作而设计、建造或使用的
senses.example: The crew lowered an underwater light to film the fish at night.
senses.exampleCN: 船员放下了一盏水下灯，在夜里拍鱼。
senses.why: Anything that has to work down there must survive pressure and water, so the word marks equipment by its place.
senses.whyCN: 凡要在那里工作的东西都得扛住水压与水，于是这个词以地点来标记器材。

senses.title: Swimming below the surface
senses.definition: moving, swimming, or staying beneath the surface rather than on it
senses.definitionCN: 在水面以下而非水面之上移动、游泳或停留
senses.example: Sea otters can swim underwater for several minutes at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 海獭一次能在水下游泳好几分钟。
senses.why: Used after a verb, the same word tells where the action happens.
senses.whyCN: 放在动词之后，同一个词说明动作发生在哪里。

senses.title: The submerged part
senses.definition: the part of a rock, hull, or structure that lies beneath the waterline
senses.definitionCN: 岩石、船体或建筑物位于水线以下的部分
senses.example: Engineers inspected the underwater of the pier for cracks.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师检查了桥墩水下部分是否有裂缝。
senses.why: The word can be turned into a noun for the hidden half of a thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以名词化，指一样东西藏在水下的那一半。

senses.title: In debt: sunk below
senses.titleCN: 资不抵债：沉到水面以下
senses.definition: in the phrase underwater on a loan, owing more than the property is worth
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 underwater on a loan，指欠款超过抵押物价值
senses.example: After the flood the family was underwater on its mortgage.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水之后，这家的房贷已经资不抵债。
senses.why: Financially the image is exact: the borrower is below the line, and the water over his head is debt.
senses.whyCN: 在财务上这个比喻很贴切：借款人沉在水线以下，头顶的水就是债。

intro.en: Underwater is a transparent English compound of two native roots, first used when people began to write about diving and the sea floor.
intro.cn: underwater 是结构透明的英语复合词，两个部件都是本土词根，人们开始描写潜水与海底时才用起来。

items.en: Under is Old English under, beneath, and wæter is the native word for water.
items.cn: under 是古英语 under（在下面），wæter 是表示水的本土词。

items.en: Both words descend from Germanic forms, and they have stood side by side since the earliest English.
items.cn: 两个词都源自日耳曼语形式，自最早的英语起就并立使用。

items.en: In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries divers wrote of underwater work on wrecks and harbours.
items.cn: 十七与十八世纪，潜水员记录关于沉船与港口的水下作业时用了这个说法。

items.en: The nineteenth century added underwater cables, tunnels and photography.
items.cn: 十九世纪又添了水下电缆、隧道与水下摄影。

items.en: The word was later borrowed by finance for debt below the value line.
items.cn: 后来金融界借用了这个词，指价值线以下的债务。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other compounds with under-; the near-meaning group gathers words for things below the surface with different scope.
note.cn: 形近组收其他以 under- 构成的复合词；近义组收表示水面以下事物的词，范围各有不同。

entries.definition: Below the surface of the ground, or the railway that runs there.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「地下的」，也指地下铁路。

entries.definition: Below the surface of the sea; close to underwater but usually about the sea only.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「海底的」，与 underwater 接近，但通常只用于海。

entries.definition: Not letting water through; describes a material rather than a place.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「防水的」，描述材料而非位置。

entries.definition: Already started and in progress; the second half is way, not water.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「已开始的、进行中的」，后半部分是 way 而不是 water。

entries.definition: Further along a river in the direction the water flows.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「下游的」，指沿水流方向更远处。

entries.definition: Completely covered by water; stresses the fact of being drowned rather than the place.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「被淹没的」，强调被水盖住的状况而非位置。

entries.definition: A vessel that travels below the surface; also an adjective for undersea things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词「潜艇」，也作形容词表示「海底的」。

entries.definition: Lying at the bottom, especially of a ship or a garden area set lower down.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「沉没的、下凹的」，多指沉船或下沉的庭院。

entries.definition: Of the open ocean far from land and far below the surface.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「深海的」，指远离陆地、水面很深的开放海域。

entries.definition: A formal adjective for life or activity below water; rare in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「水下的、水生的」，较正式，日常少见。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two plain English pieces and the real phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词的两个朴素英语部件，以及它真实出现的搭配。

normal.en: Under plus water: wherever the word goes, it names a place below the surface.
normal.cn: under 加 water：这个词无论怎么用，指的都是水面以下的位置。

normal.en: An underwater camera must survive pressure, so it is named by where it works.
normal.cn: 水下摄像机必须扛住水压，因此以工作地点命名。

normal.en: Swim underwater uses the word as an adverb after the verb.
normal.cn: swim underwater 把这个词当副词放在动词之后。

normal.en: Separate the two words and under water means flooded, not undersea.
normal.cn: 分开写 under water 表示被水淹了，而不是在海底。

normal.en: Being underwater on a mortgage means owing more than the house is worth.
normal.cn: underwater on a mortgage 指欠的钱比房子价值还多。

abstract.en: Picture the waterline as a strict border: everything under it lives by different rules of light, sound and weight.
abstract.cn: 把水线想象成一条严格的边界：线以下的一切按另一套光、声与重量的规则生活。

abstract.en: The same word covers a camera, a reef and a debt, because all three have sunk below a line other people set.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指相机、礁石也指债务，因为三者都沉到了别人划出的某条线以下。

abstract.en: Underwater is not simply wet: it is a whole layer of the world with its own name.
abstract.cn: underwater 不只是「湿」：它是世界的一整个层次，有自己的名字。

examples.en: The underwater cave is home to blind fish and pale shrimp.
examples.cn: 这个水下洞穴里住着盲鱼和苍白的虾。

examples.en: He can hold his breath underwater for nearly two minutes.
examples.cn: 他在水下能憋气将近两分钟。

examples.en: Repair crews sent an underwater robot to check the broken pipe.
examples.cn: 维修队派出水下机器人检查破裂的管道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的渥特」——安潜到渥特河的水面以下：水下的

root: 由古英语 under（在下面）与 wæter（水）两个日耳曼语系本土词构成，字面就是「在水之下」；近代随潜水、海底工程与水下摄影而广泛使用，后来又借到金融里指资不抵债。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of underwater all keep one relation: something lies below the surface of water, whether it is a place, a tool, a movement, a hidden part, or a debt.
sensesIntro.cn: underwater 的五个义项都维持同一种关系：某物位于水面以下，无论那是地点、器材、动作、隐藏的部分还是债务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a diver sinks through the bright surface into a green, quiet world below.
core.cn: 核心意象：潜水者穿过明亮的水面，沉入下方青绿而安静的世界。

branches.en: THE PLACE: whatever is under the surface is described by one word.
branches.cn: 地点线：凡是水面以下的事物都用这一个词描述。

branches.en: THE GEAR: cameras, lights and robots are named by where they must work.
branches.cn: 器材线：相机、灯与机器人都以必须工作的地方命名。

branches.en: THE MOTION: swimming beneath the surface uses the word as an adverb.
branches.cn: 动作线：在水面以下游泳时，这个词作副词用。

branches.en: THE HIDDEN HALF: a hull or a pier has an underwater part no one sees.
branches.cn: 隐藏线：船体或桥墩都有没人看得见的水下部分。

branches.en: THE DEBT: finance borrows the image for owing more than the value line.
branches.cn: 债务线：金融借用这个意象，指欠款超过价值线。

intro.en: Both halves of underwater are native English words, so the word has no Latin core at all.
intro.cn: underwater 的两半都是英语本土词，因此这个词完全没有拉丁词根核心。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element here; the table below lists only the later Latin-based synonyms that name the same place.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分；下表只列出后世以拉丁语为源、指同一位置的近义词。

items.example: The prefix fixes the position below the surface.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀锁定水面以下的位置。

items.meaning: the liquid of seas and rivers
items.example: The noun names the medium that covers the thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指覆盖该物的介质。

items.example: It appears in submerged and submarine.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 submerged 与 submarine 中。

items.example: It stresses being drowned rather than being below.
items.exampleCN: 它强调被水盖住而非位置在下面。

items.example: It uses sub plus marinus, of the sea.
items.exampleCN: 它由 sub 加表示「海的」marinus 构成。
underwater 的一个范围更窄的近亲。

items.example: The word is fully native in both halves.
items.exampleCN: 这个词的两半都是完全的英语本土成分。

items.meaning: the line where water touches a hull
items.example: The border that underwater refers to.
items.exampleCN: 正是 underwater 所指的那条界线。

definition_zh: 无疑地；毫无疑问；确实
definition_en: used to say that something is certainly true
core_image: 问题一出口，全场没有一个摇头的人
scene: 讲座结束时，主持人问在场有没有人反对这个结论，礼堂里安静了几秒，没有人举手。This is undoubtedly the best solution available.
sceneCN: 这里 undoubtedly 是「毫无疑问」（第 1 个义项：表达确定无疑）；句意为这无疑是目前最好的办法。全场无人摇头，正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ly 的形容词，义为「无疑的；公认的」
同源名词，义为「怀疑」
同源形容词，义为「怀疑的；可疑的」

senses.title: Beyond any doubt
senses.definition: used to state that something is certainly true
senses.definitionCN: 用于表明某事确实成立
senses.example: The bridge is undoubtedly the finest in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥无疑是这一带最好的。
senses.why: The adverb is un- plus doubt plus -ed plus -ly, a stack of four pieces saying not doubted at all.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词是 un-、doubt、-ed、-ly 四层叠成，意思就是「一点也没被怀疑」。

senses.title: Used as a hedge in careful writing
senses.definition: used to soften a strong claim while keeping it firm
senses.definitionCN: 用来在保持坚持的同时稍微软化断言
senses.example: Undoubtedly, some details will change.
senses.exampleCN: 显然，有些细节会变。
senses.why: Formal writers like a small pause before the claim, and the adverb supplies it without weakening the claim.
senses.whyCN: 正式写作者喜欢在断言前留一小顿，这个副词在不减弱断言的前提下提供了那一顿。

senses.title: Used for emphasis on a prediction
senses.definition: placed before will to strengthen a forecast
senses.definitionCN: 放在 will 之前加强预测
senses.example: Prices will undoubtedly rise again.
senses.exampleCN: 价格必然会再次上涨。
senses.why: A forecast has no evidence in the present, so the word lends it borrowed certainty.
senses.whyCN: 预测在当下没有证据，这个词便借给它一份确定。

senses.title: Used for emphasis before a superlative
senses.definition: placed before a superlative to confirm the ranking
senses.definitionCN: 放在最高级前确认这一排名
senses.example: She is undoubtedly the most patient of the three.
senses.exampleCN: 她无疑是三人中最有耐心的。
senses.why: A superlative already claims the top, and the adverb confirms that nobody will dispute it.
senses.whyCN: 最高级本身已占住顶端，这个副词只是确认无人会提出异议。

senses.title: In the manner of something not doubted
senses.definition: of a fact, in a way that nobody questions
senses.definitionCN: 就某事实而言，无人质疑地
senses.example: His courage was undoubtedly real.
senses.exampleCN: 他的勇气无疑是真实的。
senses.why: The strength always sits in the doubting that is being denied.
senses.whyCN: 力量始终来自被否定掉的那份怀疑。

intro.en: The word is a four-part English stack on a Latin verb of doubting.
intro.cn: 这个词是四层英语叠加，底座是拉丁语的「怀疑」动词。

items.en: Dubitare means to waver between two things, related to duo, two.
items.cn: dubitare 意为在两者之间摇摆，与 duo（二）相关。

items.en: Old French douter carries the sense of fearing and questioning.
items.cn: 古法语 douter 带出「畏惧、存疑」之义。

items.en: Doubt enters English, and the adjective undoubted adds un- to deny it.
items.cn: doubt 进入英语后，形容词 undoubted 加 un- 加以否认。

items.en: The adverb undoubtedly is formed with -ly and becomes frequent in formal prose.
items.cn: 副词 undoubtedly 加 -ly 而成，在正式文章中频繁出现。

items.en: Modern usage often places it at the start of a sentence as a confident opener.
items.cn: 现代用法常把它放在句首，作为有把握的开场。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the doubt family, and the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of certainty.
note.cn: 形近组共用 doubt 词族，近义组汇集表示确定的副词。

entries.definition: a feeling of not being sure
unsure or unlikely
not questioned
without any doubt
in a clear and sure way
possibly, as can be argued
maybe

normalIntro.en: Un- denies the doubt, -ed frames it as a settled fact, and -ly makes it an adverb.
normalIntro.cn: un- 否定怀疑，-ed 把它说成既成事实，-ly 再把它变成副词。

normal.en: Dubitare means to waver between two things, so undoubted means no wavering at all.
normal.cn: dubitare 意为在两者间摇摆，undoubted 就是完全不摇摆。

normal.en: Undoubtedly and undoubtedly true are both common, the second adding emphasis.
normal.cn: undoubtedly 与 undoubtedly true 都常见，后者再加一层强调。

normal.en: In careful writing it softens a claim without giving it up.
normal.cn: 在严谨写作里它软化断言，却不放弃断言。

normal.en: Before will and before a superlative it works as a firm support.
normal.cn: 放在 will 与最高级之前，它起稳固的支撑作用。

normal.en: The adjective form undoubted is rarer but appears in formal prose.
normal.cn: 形容词形式 undoubted 较少用，但见于正式文章。

abstract.en: Ask a room for objections and watch no hand go up.
abstract.cn: 向一屋子人问有没有异议，看没有一只手举起来。

abstract.en: Hear the pause that grows heavier than any answer.
abstract.cn: 听那阵沉默比任何回答都更沉。

abstract.en: Then place that certainty in front of a claim and walk away.
abstract.cn: 再把这份确定放在一句论断前面，转身走开。

examples.en: The discovery is undoubtedly important for farmers.
examples.cn: 这一发现对农民无疑很重要。

examples.en: She is undoubtedly the strongest player in the team.
examples.cn: 她无疑是队里最强的选手。

examples.en: The news will undoubtedly spread by morning.
examples.cn: 这消息到早上必然会传开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的闹特得利」——心里安，闹不清楚的（not）东西都理得利落，自然无疑。

root: un-（否定）+ doubt（拉丁语 dubitare「摇摆不定」，与 duo「二」同源）+ -ed + -ly；现多作副词 undoubted + -ly

sensesIntro.en: One meaning at bottom: the doubt that would normally be there is not there.
sensesIntro.cn: 归根到底只有一个意思：本该出现的怀疑并未出现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a question asked and no hand raised.
core.cn: 核心意象：问题问出，无人举手。

branches.en: The certain branch: a plain statement of fact.
branches.cn: 确定分支：对事实的平实陈述。

branches.en: The hedge branch: softening a claim without dropping it.
branches.cn: 缓和分支：软化而不放弃。

branches.en: The forecast branch: certainty about the future.
branches.cn: 预测分支：对未来的确定。

branches.en: The ranking branch: confirming a superlative.
branches.cn: 排序分支：确认最高级。

branches.en: The everyday use before a plain adjective.
branches.cn: 接普通形容词的日常用法。

intro.en: Four English layers over a Latin verb of wavering.
intro.cn: 四层英语部件叠在一个拉丁语「摇摆」动词上。

latinIntro.en: Dubitare also lies behind dubious and doubt.
latinIntro.cn: dubitare 还支撑着 dubious 与 doubt。

items.example: She was doubtful of the plan.

items.exampleCN: 她无可置疑的技艺令我们佩服。

definition_zh: 不安的；心神不宁的；不自在的；令人不安的；不稳定的
definition_en: slightly worried or uncomfortable, or making people feel that something is wrong
core_image: 坐在椅子上却怎么也找不到一个安稳的姿势
scene: 深夜的病房里，家人守着还没出结果的化验单，谁也坐不住。The silence in the waiting room made everyone uneasy.
sceneCN: 这里 uneasy 是「心神不宁的」（第 1 个义项：心里不踏实）；句意为候诊室里的沉默让每个人都坐立不安。找不到安稳姿势的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不安地；局促地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不安；局促」
去掉否定前缀 un- 后的肯定形式，义为「容易的；从容的」

senses.title: Feeling worried without a clear reason
senses.definition: slightly worried or nervous, often without being able to say why
senses.definitionCN: 有点担心或紧张，往往说不出具体缘由
senses.example: She felt uneasy about the phone call and could not sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 她为那通电话感到不安，翻来覆去睡不着。
senses.why: The prefix means not, and the base word means at ease, so uneasy is literally not at ease.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 表示「不」，词根本义是「安逸、自在」，因此 uneasy 字面上就是「不自在」，不安从这里直接生出。

senses.title: Awkward in company
senses.definition: not comfortable in a social situation, as if you do not know what to do with yourself
senses.definitionCN: 在社交场合中不舒服，手脚都不知往哪里放
senses.example: He gave an uneasy laugh and changed the subject.
senses.exampleCN: 他局促地笑了一下，换了个话题。
senses.why: The same lack of ease that keeps the body restless also shows in a voice or a laugh.
senses.whyCN: 让身体坐立难安的那份不自在，同样会从嗓音和笑声里露出来。

senses.title: A silence or mood that suggests trouble
senses.definition: used of a silence, mood, or peace that seems to hide a problem
senses.definitionCN: 形容沉默、气氛或和平似乎掩盖着问题
senses.example: An uneasy silence fell over the table after his remark.
senses.exampleCN: 他那一句话之后，桌上一片令人不安的沉默。
senses.why: A feeling of not being at ease spreads from people to the room they sit in.
senses.whyCN: 不自在的感觉会从人传到人所在的屋子，于是空气本身也显得不安。

senses.title: A relationship or arrangement that may not last
senses.definition: used of a peace, alliance, or agreement that is forced and may break down
senses.definitionCN: 形容被迫达成、随时可能破裂的和平、联盟或协议
senses.example: The two sides reached an uneasy truce before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 双方在入冬前达成了勉强的停战。
senses.why: Anything that leaves people not at ease is also likely to fall apart.
senses.whyCN: 任何让人无法安心的安排，往往也难以长久维持。

senses.title: Sleep that is broken and shallow
senses.definition: used of sleep that is light and full of waking moments
senses.definitionCN: 形容睡得浅、常常醒来的睡眠
senses.example: After a night of uneasy sleep she went back to the hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 睡了一夜不踏实的觉，她又回到了医院。
senses.why: The body that cannot settle by day cannot settle at night either.
senses.whyCN: 白天找不到安稳姿势的身体，夜里同样安稳不下来。

intro.en: The word is a plain English construction: un- plus easy, with the mental sense of easy coming from Old French.
intro.cn: 这个词是地道的英语构造：un- 加 easy，而 easy 的「安逸」之义来自古法语。

items.en: The prefix un- was already used to reverse the meaning of a word.
items.cn: 古英语时期，前缀 un- 已用于反转词义。

items.en: Aise meant comfort or leisure, and the phrase at ease entered English from it.
items.cn: aise 意为「舒适、闲暇」，短语 at ease 由此进入英语。

items.en: Ease and easy grew from that source and meant free from pain or trouble.
items.cn: ease 与 easy 由这一来源发展而来，意为「无痛无扰」。

items.en: Uneasy is formed by adding the negative prefix to easy and appears in writing in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: uneasy 由否定前缀加 easy 构成，十六世纪见于书面记录。

items.en: The sense widens to silences, alliances, and sleep, wherever a calm surface hides strain.
items.cn: 此后意义扩展到沉默、联盟与睡眠，只要平静的表面下藏着紧张就能用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other un- adjectives about attitude, while the near-meaning group collects words for fear.
note.cn: 形近组收集其他表示态度的 un- 形容词，近义组汇集表示担忧害怕的词。

entries.definition: not difficult, or free from worry
in a worried or awkward way
not firm or stable
entries.definitionCN: 不稳的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: not common
entries.definitionCN: 不寻常的（只是前缀相同，词根不同）

entries.definition: worried about what may happen
unable to stay still
slightly frightened or tense
peaceful and not worried

normalIntro.en: Nothing in the word is exotic: a negative prefix rests on a word for comfort.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词一点也不生僻：一个否定前缀压在一个表示舒适的词上。

normal.en: Un- plus easy: not at ease is exactly what uneasy means.
normal.cn: un- 加 easy：不在自在的状态，就是 uneasy 的本义。

normal.en: Feel uneasy about something is the most common frame for learners.
normal.cn: feel uneasy about 是学习者最常用的搭配框架。

normal.en: Uneasiness is the state, uneasily the manner of moving or speaking.
normal.cn: uneasiness 是那种状态，uneasily 是那种说话或动作的样子。

normal.en: An uneasy silence and an uneasy alliance both point to tension under the surface.
normal.cn: an uneasy silence 与 an uneasy alliance 都指向表面之下的紧张。

normal.en: Compare at ease, which means relaxed, to see the negative in action.
normal.cn: 对比 at ease（放松、自在）就能看清否定前缀的作用。

abstract.en: Picture hands on a chair arm, fingers tapping and stopping.
abstract.cn: 想象一双手搭在椅臂上，手指敲了又停。

abstract.en: Hear a joke, then a laugh one beat too late.
abstract.cn: 听一个笑话，然后是一声慢了半拍的笑。

abstract.en: Feel a room where everyone has decided not to say the obvious thing.
abstract.cn: 体会一个所有人都绕着明摆着的话说的房间。

examples.en: He was uneasy about leaving his mother alone in the house.
examples.cn: 他不放心把母亲一个人留在家里。

examples.en: An uneasy calm settled on the village after the storm.
examples.cn: 风暴过后，村子笼罩在一片令人不安的平静里。

examples.en: She smiled uneasily at the doctor and closed the door behind her.
examples.cn: 她对医生不安地笑笑，然后关上了身后的门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺意贼」——钱包里少了钱，俺心里就惦记着那个贼，坐也坐不稳。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 un-（不）+ easy（安逸的），easy 义源自旧法语 aise（舒适、闲暇），短语 at ease 即由此而来

sensesIntro.en: A single state, not being at ease, spreads from the body to voices, rooms, agreements, and sleep.
sensesIntro.cn: 一份状态，不自在，从身体蔓延到嗓音、房间、协议与睡眠。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body that cannot find a settled position.
core.cn: 核心意象：一副怎么也摆不稳的身体。

branches.en: The private branch: a vague worry with no clear cause.
branches.cn: 私密分支：说不出缘由的隐约担忧。

branches.en: The social branch: the body that does not know how to stand.
branches.cn: 社交分支：身体不知该怎么摆。

branches.en: The atmosphere branch: a room that hints at a hidden problem.
branches.cn: 气氛分支：屋子暗示着藏起来的问题。

branches.en: The arrangement branch: a peace everyone expects to break.
branches.cn: 安排分支：人人都知道待不住的和平。

branches.en: The nightly branch: sleep that keeps coming apart.
branches.cn: 夜间分支：总是断开的睡眠。

intro.en: The word is built from a negative prefix and a borrowed adjective, so its parts are easy to read.
intro.cn: 这个词由否定前缀与借入的形容词搭成，部件一眼可辨。

latinIntro.en: The base word is not Latin, but the Old French aise behind it may come from Latin adjacens, lying near.
latinIntro.cn: 词根本身不是拉丁语，但其后的旧法语 aise 可能源自拉丁语 adjacens（邻近的）。

items.example: Uneasy means not easy in comfort.
He glanced uneasily at the door.

items.exampleCN: 一种奇怪的不安充满了她。

definition_zh: 失业的；无业的；未被使用的；闲置的
definition_en: without a paid job, or not being put to use
core_image: 工作台上收起的工具，主人没有活可干
scene: 清晨的人才市场门口，几个中年人抱着简历站着，等一张招工的牌子。He has been unemployed since the factory closed.
sceneCN: 这里 unemployed 是「失业的」（第 1 个义项：没有工作）；句意为工厂关门以后他一直失业。收起工具、无活可干的画面正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ment 构成名词，义为「失业；失业率」
去掉否定前缀的动词，义为「雇用；使用」
动词加 -ee 构成的施受名词，义为「雇员」
动词加 -ment 构成名词，义为「就业；雇用」

senses.title: Without a paid job
senses.definition: not having a job that brings in money, usually while still able to work
senses.definitionCN: 没有一份挣钱的工作，通常指仍有劳动能力的人
senses.example: Two thousand workers were left unemployed by the closure.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂关闭让两千名工人失业。
senses.why: The prefix undoes the verb employ, so a person who is not employed is simply outside a job.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 把动词 employ（雇用）反转，不被雇用的人自然就落在工作之外。

senses.title: Registered as out of work
senses.definition: officially counted as looking for work and not currently having any
senses.definitionCN: 官方统计中算作正在找工作、目前没有工作的人
senses.example: He was unemployed for eight months before the interview call came.
senses.exampleCN: 他失业了八个月才等到面试通知。
senses.why: The same reversal takes on a statistical edge once governments count who is in and out of work.
senses.whyCN: 当政府开始统计谁在岗谁不在岗，这份反转就有了统计上的含义。

senses.title: The group of people without work
senses.definition: used with the as a collective noun for all people out of work
senses.definitionCN: 与 the 连用作集合名词，指全体失业的人
senses.example: The city opened a centre to help the unemployed find training.
senses.exampleCN: 市里开设了一个中心，帮失业者寻找培训机会。
senses.why: An adjective applied to many people becomes a standing label for the whole group.
senses.whyCN: 一个形容词加在许多人身上，就成了指代整个群体的固定称呼。

senses.title: Tools or money not being used
senses.definition: used of machines, money, or skills that are available but not put to work
senses.definitionCN: 形容机器、资金或技能虽可用却未被投入使用
senses.example: The mill stood idle, its machinery unemployed for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 那座磨坊停着，机器闲置了十年。
senses.why: If employ means to put to use, then anything not put to use is just as unemployed as a worker.
senses.whyCN: 既然 employ 也有「使用」之义，那么没有被使用的东西就和工人一样处于 unemployed 的状态。

senses.title: Time or energy going to waste
senses.definition: used figuratively of abilities or time that have no outlet
senses.definitionCN: 比喻性地形容才能或时间无处发挥
senses.example: Her skills lay unemployed while she cared for her father.
senses.exampleCN: 照顾父亲的那几年，她的本事无处施展。
senses.why: The picture of a capable person outside work easily transfers to abilities outside use.
senses.whyCN: 一个有能力的人被挡在工作之外的画面，很容易挪到被闲置的才能上。

intro.en: Employ comes from Latin through French, and the negative adjective is a later English addition.
intro.cn: employ 经由法语来自拉丁语，带否定前缀的形容词则是后来英语自己加上的。

items.en: Implicare meant to enfold or involve, built from in- and plicare, to fold.
items.cn: implicare 意为「裹住、卷入」，由 in- 与 plicare（折叠）构成。

items.en: Emploier developed the sense of using something or someone for a purpose.
items.cn: emploier 发展出「为某目的使用某物或某人」的意思。

items.en: English took the verb as employ, first meaning to apply or use.
items.cn: 英语借入动词作 employ，最初意为「应用、使用」。

items.en: The sense of hiring someone for wages became the dominant one by the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，「付工资雇用」成为主要义项。

items.en: Un- was added to the past participle employed to describe those without work.
items.cn: 在过去分词 employed 前加 un-，用来指没有工作的人。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the employ family, while the near-meaning group gathers words about lacking a job.
note.cn: 形近组是 employ 词族，近义组汇集表示没有工作的词。

entries.definition: the state of having paid work
a person who is paid to work for others
a person or firm that pays others to work
not yet examined
entries.definitionCN: 未勘探的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: without a job
not working or being used
no longer needed for a job
having paid work

normalIntro.en: The word is a verb with a lid on it: employ means to use or hire, un- takes that away.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个被盖上否定盖子的动词：employ 是使用或雇用，un- 则把它拿走。

normal.en: Un- plus employed: not hired, not in use.
normal.cn: un- 加 employed：没被雇用，没被使用。

normal.en: The unemployed is a collective phrase and takes a plural verb sense in British use.
normal.cn: the unemployed 是集合说法，英式用法中带复数意味。

normal.en: Unemployment is the noun, and it is the word on news reports.
normal.cn: 名词是 unemployment，也是新闻里常见的词。

normal.en: Employ, employer, employee form a neat trio of verb, giver, receiver.
normal.cn: employ、employer、employee 组成动词、给方、受方的整齐三件套。

normal.en: Idle machinery and unemployed capital share the same logic of not being put to work.
normal.cn: 闲置的机器与闲着的资金，逻辑相同，都是没被投入使用。

abstract.en: Picture a factory gate at dawn with nobody walking in.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明的厂门口，没有人往里走。

abstract.en: See a toolbox closed on a bench, dust on the lid.
abstract.cn: 看工作台上合起的工具箱，盖子上落着灰。

abstract.en: Hear a phone that does not ring for weeks.
abstract.cn: 听一部几个星期不响的电话。

examples.en: She has been unemployed since the restaurant closed last spring.
examples.cn: 自去年春天餐馆关门后她就一直失业。

examples.en: The government promised new training for the unemployed.
examples.cn: 政府承诺为失业者提供新的培训。

examples.en: His years of experience sat unemployed while he looked after the children.
examples.cn: 照顾孩子的那几年，他的经验无处施展。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺木扑落的」——活儿没了，俺木头一样扑落在地上，闲着没事干。

root: 前缀 un-（不）+ 过去分词 employed，employ 源自拉丁语 implicare（裹住、卷入），经古法语 emploier 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One reversal, not put to work, covers people, machines, money, and even talents.
sensesIntro.cn: 一次反转，「未被投入使用」，覆盖人、机器、资金乃至才能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tool box closed on a bench because there is no work to do.
core.cn: 核心意象：因为没活可干而合上的工具箱。

branches.en: The personal branch: the man at the gate and the figure in the statistics.
branches.cn: 个人分支：站在厂门口的人与统计表里的人。

branches.en: The collective branch: a phrase that names a whole group.
branches.cn: 集合分支：指称整个群体的固定说法。

branches.en: The equipment branch: machines and money standing still.
branches.cn: 器物分支：停着不动的机器和资金。

branches.en: The figurative branch: ability with nowhere to go.
branches.cn: 比喻分支：无处施展的本事。

branches.en: The plain description most learners meet first in the news.
branches.cn: 学习者最先在新闻里遇到的最朴素义项。

intro.en: The word is an English prefix on a French verb, so reading the parts is straightforward.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语前缀加法语动词，拆开看部件很直接。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb implicare lies behind the French form and supplies the oldest layer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 implicare 藏在其后，是最早的一层。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或行为的名词后缀
表示受事者的名词后缀

items.meaning: the state of having no job
having the worn look of the jobless
items.example: A shabby, unemployed-looking coat hung by the door.
items.exampleCN: 门边挂着一件像失业者穿的破旧外套。

definition_zh: 失业；失业状态；失业人数；失业率
definition_en: the state of having no job and looking for work, or the number of people in that state
core_image: 工厂大门紧闭，一群人抱着简历站在门外，门上的招聘牌被撤了下来
scene: 冬天下着小雪，镇上的纺织厂在清晨贴出停产通知，工人们围在门口不肯散去。Unemployment in the town doubled within a single winter.
sceneCN: 这里 unemployment 是「失业、失业状况」（第 1 个义项：没有工作并正在找工作）；句意为这个镇的失业人数在一个冬天里翻了一倍。关着的厂门与门外的人，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由 un- 加 employed 构成，义为「失业的；未被利用的」
由拉丁语 implicare 经法语构成，义为「雇用；使用」
由 employ 加 -ment 构成，义为「就业；雇用」
由 employ 加 -er 构成，义为「雇主」

senses.title: The state of having no work
senses.definition: the situation of being without a paid job while wanting and looking for one
senses.definitionCN: 没有有偿工作而仍希望并寻找工作的处境
senses.example: Unemployment among young graduates rose sharply last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年年轻的大学毕业生失业率急剧上升。
senses.why: Un- strips away the thing that employ gives, and -ment names the state that is left.
senses.whyCN: un- 把 employ 所给的东西拿掉，-ment 命名剩下的那个状态。

senses.title: The jobless counted together
senses.definition: the number or proportion of people in a country or area who have no work
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家或地区中没有工作的人数或比例
senses.example: The government reported that unemployment had reached nine percent.
senses.exampleCN: 政府报告称失业率已达到百分之九。
senses.why: Statistics turned the personal situation into a public figure that can be measured month by month.
senses.whyCN: 统计数据把个人处境变成了可逐月衡量的公共数字。

senses.title: Money for those without work
senses.definition: in British English, money paid by the state to people who have no job
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语中，国家付给没有工作的人的钱
senses.example: He was on unemployment for six months before finding factory work.
senses.exampleCN: 在找到工厂的工作之前，他领了六个月的失业救济。
senses.why: The abstract state became a concrete payment, as names for hard conditions often do.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的状态变成了具体的给付，描述艰难处境的名称常常这样转义。

senses.title: A machine or field out of production
senses.definition: of land, machinery, or capital: lying unused while it could be productive
senses.definitionCN: 土地、机器或资本本可发挥作用却处于闲置状态
senses.example: Economists noted the unemployment of the mills and the warehouses beside them.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家指出了那些闲置的磨坊以及旁边的仓库。
senses.why: The word can be taken literally: any resource that no one has put to work is unemployed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可按字面理解：任何没有被投入使用的资源都是「失业」的。

senses.title: A social problem by a name
senses.titleCN: 一个作为社会问题的名称
senses.definition: used as a heading for the social and political problem caused by mass joblessness
senses.definitionCN: 用作一个标题式说法，指大规模无工作所造成的社会与政治问题
senses.example: The report treated unemployment as the town's deepest and most difficult problem.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把失业视为这个镇最深、最难解决的问题。
senses.why: A word about individuals became a topic for policy: the same state, seen from above.
senses.whyCN: 一个关于个人的词变成了政策议题：同一个状态，换到高处去看。

intro.en: Unemployment is a modern English construction: a negative prefix and a set of English and French suffixes around a Latin verb.
intro.cn: unemployment 是近代英语的构造：否定前缀与一串英语、法语后缀围绕一个拉丁语动词。

items.en: Implicare meant to enfold or involve; the French verb employer took on the sense of using or engaging.
items.cn: 拉丁语 implicare 意为「包裹、卷入」；法语动词 employer 生出「使用、雇用」义。

items.en: English borrowed the French verb as employ, to use or to give work to.
items.cn: 英语借入这个法语动词作 employ，表示使用或给予工作。

items.en: The noun employer and the derived noun employment passed into English in the late Middle Ages.
items.cn: 名词 employer 与派生名词 employment 在中世纪末期进入英语。

items.en: In the nineteenth century employers and unions began to speak of unemployment as a condition of whole industries.
items.cn: 十九世纪，雇主与工会开始把失业当作整个行业的一种状况来谈论。

items.en: Measurement turned it into a statistic, and the rate of unemployment became a standard figure of public debate.
items.cn: 统计测量把它变成一项数据，失业率成为公共讨论中的标准数字。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same employ root; the near-meaning group gathers words for idleness or jobless conditions that differ in scope.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 employ 词根上的词；近义组收表示闲置或无业状况的词，范围不同。

entries.definition: The adjective for a person or resource with no work; the noun form is the state itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「失业的」，名词形式则指这种状态本身。

entries.definition: The noun for paid work itself, the opposite of unemployment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「就业、雇用」，是 unemployment 的反面。

entries.definition: A person who is hired and paid to work.
A person or company that hires others.
The act of moving troops or resources into position; close in spelling, different in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「部署」，拼写相近而意义不同。

entries.definition: The plain noun for having no job; less tied to official statistics than unemployment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「无业」，比 unemployment 更少与官方统计挂钩。

entries.definition: Job loss because a post is no longer needed; a British term, often with compensation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「裁员、冗员」，英式用法，常涉及补偿。

entries.definition: The state of not working or being unused; it can describe people or machines.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「懒散、闲置」，可用于人或机器。

entries.definition: A temporary or permanent dismissal of workers for economic reasons.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「裁员、停工解雇」，因经济原因暂时或永久辞退工人。

entries.definition: The state of working fewer hours or below one's skill level.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不充分就业」，工时不足或低于自身技能水平。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the negative prefix, the root meaning to use, and the public figures the word belongs to.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用否定前缀、表示「使用」的词根，以及这个词所归属的公共数据。

normal.en: Un- means not, employ means put to use, -ment means state: not being put to work.
normal.cn: un- 表示「不」，employ 表示「使用」，-ment 表示「状态」：不被投入使用。

normal.en: The unemployment rate is the headline figure in every budget speech.
normal.cn: 失业率是每场预算演说里的头号数据。

normal.en: In British English, to be on unemployment is to receive the jobless benefit.
normal.cn: 在英式英语里，be on unemployment 就是领取失业救济。

normal.en: Employer and employee sit on the two sides of employment.
normal.cn: 雇主与雇员站在就业的两边。

normal.en: Idle mills, empty warehouses: resources too can be unemployed.
normal.cn: 停摆的磨坊、空着的仓库：资源也会失业。

abstract.en: Picture a gate with a job notice taken down: the people outside have not changed, only the work has gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被摘下招工牌子：门外的人没有变，消失的是工作。

abstract.en: One word holds a personal winter and a national figure, because it can be counted.
abstract.cn: 一个词里同时装进一个人的冬天和一个国家的数字，因为它能被统计。

abstract.en: Unemployment names an absence, and absences are hardest to see until someone counts them.
abstract.cn: unemployment 命名的是缺失，而缺失在有人去数之前最难被看见。

examples.en: Unemployment fell for the third month in a row.
examples.cn: 失业率连续第三个月下降。

examples.en: The plant closure brought unemployment to a village that had always had work.
examples.cn: 工厂关闭使这个一向有活儿干的村子陷入失业。

examples.en: She is studying the unemployment of rural women in three provinces.
examples.cn: 她正在研究三个省份农村女性的失业问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安普洛依门特」——安没被雇主收进门：失业

root: 由 un-「不」加 employment（就业）构成；employment 源自法语 employer，再上溯拉丁语 implicare「包裹、卷入」，近代英语把「不就业的状态」独立成词，并由此生出失业人数、失业率与失业救济等用法。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of unemployment all name one absence, the lack of paid work, seen as a person's state, a statistic, a payment, an idle resource, or a public problem.
sensesIntro.cn: unemployment 的五个义项都在命名同一种缺失，即有偿工作的缺席，只是分别看作个人状态、统计数据、给付、闲置资源与公共问题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the factory gate is shut and the job notice has been taken down.
core.cn: 核心意象：工厂大门紧闭，招工启事已经被撤下。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a woman or man without paid work, still looking.
branches.cn: 个人线：没有有偿工作、仍在寻找机会的人。

branches.en: THE NUMBER: the same state counted across a region and published monthly.
branches.cn: 数字线：同一状态在地区范围内被计数并按月公布。

branches.en: THE PAYMENT: the state turns into money from the state.
branches.cn: 给付线：这种状态转成了国家给出的钱。

branches.en: THE RESOURCE: machines and land can be unemployed too.
branches.cn: 资源线：机器与土地也会处于闲置状态。

branches.en: THE AGENDA: mass joblessness becomes a topic of policy and debate.
branches.cn: 议题线：大规模无工作成为政策与争论的话题。

intro.en: Unemployment stacks a negative prefix, a Latin-derived root, and two noun suffixes, which is why it looks long.
intro.cn: unemployment 层叠了否定前缀、拉丁语来源的词根与两个名词后缀，所以看上去很长。

latinIntro.en: Latin implicare is recorded, and French employer stands between it and the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 implicare 有文献记录，法语 employer 位于它与英语词之间。

items.example: The prefix denies that work is present.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀否认工作的存在。

items.example: It marks being folded into a job or use.
items.exampleCN: 它表示被卷进一项工作或用途中。

items.example: The old root lies inside employ.
items.exampleCN: 这个古老词根藏在 employ 里面。

items.example: It appears in deployment, a look-alike word.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在形近词 deployment 中。

items.example: The Latin verb behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 整个词族背后的拉丁动词。

latinEntries.structure: Old French verb from Latin implicare

definition_zh: 意外的；出乎意料的；没有料想到的；突兀的
definition_en: not anticipated or planned, so that it surprises people
core_image: 推开门发现屋里站着一位本以为还在远方的人
scene: 生日那天，灯一直关着，门后躲着一屋子的朋友，她一进门就叫出了声。Her visit was completely unexpected.
sceneCN: 这里 unexpected 是「意外的」（第 1 个义项：事先没有想到）；句意为她来访完全出乎意料。推门见人的画面就是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「意外地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「意外性」
去掉否定前缀与原后缀的动词，义为「期待；预料」
动词加 -ation 构成名词，义为「期待；预期」

senses.title: Not what anyone thought would happen
senses.definition: not believed likely to happen, so that it takes people by surprise
senses.definitionCN: 被认为不太会发生，因而让人吃惊
senses.example: Her answer was so unexpected that no one spoke for a while.
senses.exampleCN: 她的回答太出人意料，一时间谁都没说话。
senses.why: The prefix removes the verb of looking forward, so what is not looked forward to arrives without warning.
senses.whyCN: 前缀去掉了「向前张望」这个动作，没被张望的事物就毫无预告地到来了。

senses.title: A visit or arrival nobody planned for
senses.definition: used of a guest or arrival that no one had prepared for
senses.definitionCN: 形容没有人做过准备的客人或到来
senses.example: An unexpected visitor knocked just as dinner was served.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭刚端上桌，一位不速之客敲了门。
senses.why: The most visible kind of the unlooked-for is a person at the door.
senses.whyCN: 没被预料的种种事物中，最显眼的就是站在门口的那个人。

senses.title: An outcome that differs from the forecast
senses.definition: used of a result, turn, or ending that no one predicted
senses.definitionCN: 形容没人预测到的结果、转折或结局
senses.example: The trial took an unexpected turn on the second day.
senses.exampleCN: 审判第二天出现了意外的转折。
senses.why: Expect also means to predict, so a result that escapes prediction is unexpected.
senses.whyCN: expect 也有「预测」之义，逃出预测的结果自然就是意外的。

senses.title: Sudden in a slightly awkward way
senses.definition: happening at a moment that feels awkward or poorly timed
senses.definitionCN: 发生在让人觉得尴尬或不合适的时候
senses.example: An unexpected silence made the joke fall flat.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵突兀的沉默让那个笑话落了空。
senses.why: Surprise and discomfort are neighbours, so the word often carries a hint of awkwardness.
senses.whyCN: 惊讶与不适本是邻居，因此这个词常常带着一点尴尬的意味。

senses.title: Costs that were not budgeted for
senses.definition: used of money that must be spent beyond what was planned
senses.definitionCN: 形容超出原计划必须支出的钱款
senses.example: Unexpected repairs ate up the whole holiday fund.
senses.exampleCN: 预算外的修理费吃掉了整笔度假基金。
senses.why: Whatever was not planned for will also not be budgeted for.
senses.whyCN: 凡是没被计划在内的，也就没被编进预算。

intro.en: Expect comes from Latin through French, and the negative adjective was formed in English.
intro.cn: expect 经由法语来自拉丁语，带否定前缀的形容词则是英语自己造出来的。

items.en: Exspectare meant to look out for, from ex-, out, and spectare, to look.
items.cn: exspectare 意为「向外张望」，由 ex-（向外）与 spectare（看）构成。

items.en: The verb passed into French as expecter, keeping the sense of awaiting.
items.cn: 这个动词进入法语作 expecter，保留「等候」之义。

items.en: English borrowed it as expect and used it for awaiting something with confidence.
items.cn: 英语借入作 expect，用来表示有把握地等候某事。

items.en: The sense widened to predicting or supposing what will happen.
items.cn: 其意义扩展为预测或设想将会发生的事。

items.en: Un- placed before the past participle gave a word for what nobody looked for.
items.cn: 在过去分词前加 un-，就得到了表示「没人张望过之事」的词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the expect family, and the near-meaning group gathers words for surprise.
note.cn: 形近组是 expect 词族，近义组汇集表示惊讶的词。

entries.definition: to think that something will happen
in a way nobody planned for
a belief that something will happen
not changed or influenced
entries.definitionCN: 未受影响的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: causing surprise
happening very quickly
not known in advance
known in advance to be coming

normalIntro.en: The word is a looking-forward verb with the looking taken away.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词本是「向前张望」的动词，把张望拿走了。

normal.en: Un- plus expected: not looked forward to.
normal.cn: un- 加 expected：没被张望过的。

normal.en: Expect comes from spectare, to look, which is also in spectator.
normal.cn: expect 源自 spectare（看），spectator 里也有这个词根。

normal.en: Unexpectedly is the adverb that usually sits next to arrive or happen.
normal.cn: unexpectedly 这个副词常跟在 arrive 或 happen 旁边。

normal.en: Completely unexpected is a very common intensifier pattern.
normal.cn: completely unexpected 是很常见的加强说法。

normal.en: Unexpected expenses and unexpected guests are two familiar collocations.
normal.cn: unexpected expenses 与 unexpected guests 是两个熟悉的搭配。

abstract.en: Picture a door swinging open to a room full of friends.
abstract.cn: 想象门一推开，屋里站满朋友。

definition_en: having bad luck, or being a regrettable thing to say or do
core_image: 刚出门就下雨，而伞恰好留在了家里
scene: 他赶到车站时，车门正好在眼前合上，下一班要等一小时。It was an unfortunate start to the day.
sceneCN: 这里 unfortunate 是「倒霉的、不幸的」（第 1 个义项：运气不好）；句意为这一天的开头很不顺。刚出门就下雨而伞留在家里，正是这个词的核心画面。

senses.title: Having bad luck
senses.definition: suffering from bad luck or a bad turn of events
senses.definitionCN: 遭遇坏运气或事态的不利转折
senses.example: The unfortunate passengers spent the night in the station.
senses.exampleCN: 那些倒霉的乘客在车站里过了一夜。
senses.why: The prefix negates fortune, which came from Latin fors, chance, so unfortunate means without good chance.
senses.whyCN: 前缀否定了 fortune（源自拉丁语 fors，机遇），unfortunate 就是没有好机缘。

senses.title: Regrettable rather than tragic
senses.definition: used of something mildly bad that one wishes had not happened
senses.definitionCN: 形容某件不太好、但愿没有发生的事
senses.example: It is unfortunate that the meeting falls on a public holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 会议恰逢公共假日，真是可惜。
senses.why: Bad luck on a small scale is simply a pity, so the word softens into regret.
senses.whyCN: 小尺度的坏运气就只是「可惜」，于是这个词软化成遗憾。

senses.title: Said of a person who deserves sympathy
senses.definition: used to describe someone who has been badly treated or badly served
senses.definitionCN: 形容受到苛待或委屈而值得同情的人
senses.example: He was unfortunate enough to be standing nearest the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他倒霉到刚好站在门边。
senses.why: Chance picks its victims without reason, and the word marks whoever chance picked.
senses.whyCN: 机遇挑人从不讲理由，这个词就标记出被挑中的那一个。

senses.title: Words or actions in poor taste
senses.definition: used of a remark or choice that is awkward and causes offence by accident
senses.definitionCN: 形容某句话或某个选择不巧令人不快，并非有意
senses.example: An unfortunate remark ruined the toast.
senses.exampleCN: 一句不恰当的玩笑毁掉了那番祝酒。
senses.why: A choice that brings bad consequences feels like bad luck even when it was your own.
senses.whyCN: 一个带来坏后果的选择，即使出于自己，也像坏运气一般。

senses.title: A combination of events that go wrong together
senses.definition: used of a coincidence or set of conditions that produce a bad outcome
senses.definitionCN: 形容若干条件凑在一起造成坏结果的巧合
senses.example: An unfortunate combination of wind and rain delayed the flight.
senses.exampleCN: 风雨不幸地凑在一起，让航班延误了。
senses.why: When several chances line up badly, the whole arrangement carries the label.
senses.whyCN: 当几个偶然凑得极糟，整个组合都带上了这个标签。

intro.en: Fortune comes from Latin through French, and English made the negative adjective with un-.
intro.cn: fortune 经由法语来自拉丁语，英语自己用 un- 造出否定形容词。

items.en: Fortuna was the goddess of chance, from fors, meaning luck or accident.
items.cn: Fortuna 是掌管机运的女神，出自 fors，意为「运气、偶然」。

items.en: Fortune entered French as a word for chance and what chance brings.
items.cn: fortune 进入法语，指机遇以及机遇带来的东西。

items.en: English borrowed fortune, which also came to mean wealth.
items.cn: 英语借入 fortune，后来又引申为财富。

items.en: Fortunate was formed from fortune, and un- was prefixed to it.
items.cn: fortunate 由 fortune 派生，再被加上前缀 un-。

items.en: The adjective softens into pity and mild regret in modern usage.
items.cn: 现代用法中，这个形容词软化为同情与轻微的遗憾。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the fortune family, and the near-meaning group gathers words of bad luck.
note.cn: 形近组是 fortune 词族，近义组汇集表示不幸的词。

normal.cn: unfortunately 常作句首语，unfortunate 用来描述人或事。

normal.cn: fortune 还表示财富，同出「机遇」这一观念。

abstract.cn: 想象跑者刚跑到站台，车门正好合上。

abstract.cn: 看野餐布铺开，天色却正要变坏。

abstract.cn: 听一个笑话只差一个词就落空。

examples.cn: 这个不幸的家庭同时失去了房子和车子。

sensesIntro.cn: 把机缘好的一面去掉，从真正的困厄一直延伸到一句不巧的话。

core.cn: 核心意象：刚下雨时，伞恰好留在家里。

definition_zh: 不幸地；遗憾的是；不巧；可惜
definition_en: in a way that is bad luck or a cause of regret, often used to open a sentence
core_image: 话还没说完，先一声轻轻的叹气
scene: 电话那头安静了一会儿，然后才传来婉拒的答复。Unfortunately, the tickets were already gone.
sceneCN: 这里 unfortunately 是「遗憾的是」（第 2 个义项：表示惋惜的评注）；句意为可惜票已经卖完了。一声先于说话的叹气，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 副词去掉 -ly 的形容词形式，义为「不幸的」

senses.title: By bad luck
senses.definition: by an unlucky turn of events rather than by anyone fault
senses.definitionCN: 由于事态的不巧转折，而非任何人的过错
senses.example: Unfortunately, the rain started just as the ceremony began.
senses.exampleCN: 不巧的是，仪式刚开始就下起了雨。
senses.why: The adverb returns to the oldest sense of fortune as chance and says the chance went wrong.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词回到 fortune 最古老的「机遇」之义，只是说机遇走坏了。

senses.title: Regrettably, used as a comment
senses.definition: used at the start of a clause to soften bad or unwelcome news
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，用来软化坏消息或不那么受欢迎的答复
senses.example: Unfortunately, we cannot offer you the position.
senses.exampleCN: 很遗憾，这个职位我们无法录用你。
senses.why: A word of bad chance placed outside the sentence turns into a polite frame for news.
senses.whyCN: 被放到句子外面的「坏运气」，就成了一种通报消息的礼貌包装。

senses.title: At a badly chosen moment
senses.definition: used of something that happens at an awkward time
senses.definitionCN: 形容某事发生在很尴尬的时间点
senses.example: The announcement came unfortunately close to the election.
senses.exampleCN: 这项宣布来得离选举太近，很不凑巧。
senses.why: Timing is part of chance, so a bad hour is a small piece of bad fortune.
senses.whyCN: 时机本是机遇的一部分，因此一个坏时刻就是一小片坏运气。

senses.title: With real loss or hardship
senses.definition: used when the outcome involves genuine harm to someone
senses.definitionCN: 用于结果确实对某人造成伤害的场合
senses.example: Unfortunately, the files had not been saved.
senses.exampleCN: 不幸的是，那些文件没有保存。
senses.why: The mild and the grave uses sit on one scale, and only the context sets the weight.
senses.whyCN: 轻重两种用法在同一条刻度上，只有语境才决定它的分量。

senses.title: In a reply, as a soft no
senses.definition: used in conversation as a gentle way of refusing or correcting
senses.definitionCN: 在对话中委婉地拒绝或纠正他人
senses.example: Unfortunately not, the shop closes at six.
senses.exampleCN: 抱歉不行，那家店六点就关门了。
senses.why: Polite refusals borrow the language of chance so that nobody takes the blame.
senses.whyCN: 委婉的拒绝借用了「运气」的说法，好让谁都不必担责。

normal.en: Un- plus fortunately: by bad luck.
normal.cn: un- 加 fortunately：运气不好。

normal.en: It almost always comes first in its clause, followed by a comma.
normal.cn: 它几乎总在小句开头，后面加一个逗号。

normal.en: Unfortunately not is a common soft refusal in speech.
normal.cn: unfortunately not 是口语中常见的委婉拒绝。

normal.en: Fortunately is the buoyant twin used for good outcomes.
normal.cn: fortunately 是它的乐观孪生词，用于好结果。

normal.en: Unfortunately for someone narrows the bad luck to one person.

definition_zh: 制服；校服；军服；统一的；一律的；一致的
definition_en: the special clothes worn by members of a school, service, or team, or being the same in every part
core_image: 一排学生穿着同一款式同一颜色同一尺码的校服，站成一条整齐的直线
scene: 开学第一天，校门口有位女老师拿着尺子检查每个人的衣领和袖口。Every student wore the same blue uniform, down to the buttons.
sceneCN: 这里 uniform 是「校服、制服」（第 1 个义项：同一团体成员穿的同款服装）；句意为每个学生都穿着同样的蓝色校服，连纽扣都一样。排成一排的同款衣服，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 均匀的；无变化的（速度、质地）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「一致地；均匀地」
由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「一致性；一律」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「穿制服的」
由本词加 -less 构成，义为「没有制服的」

senses.title: Clothes that mark a group
senses.definition: a set of clothes that all members of a school, service, or team wear
senses.definitionCN: 某学校、部队或团队的成员全部穿着的成套服装
senses.example: Nurses at the city hospital wear a white uniform.
senses.exampleCN: 市医院的护士穿白色制服。
senses.why: Uni- is one and form is shape: one shape of dress for many bodies.
senses.whyCN: uni- 是「一」，form 是「形状」：许多身体只穿一种形状的衣服。

senses.title: The same in every part
senses.definition: being the same in size, style, or rules everywhere, without variation
senses.definitionCN: 在尺寸、样式或规则上处处相同，没有变化
senses.example: All branches follow a uniform set of safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 所有分店都遵循一套统一的安全规则。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the very image of the clothes: one form applied everywhere.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留的正是衣服的意象：一种形式被用到处处。

senses.title: Steady and even
senses.definition: remaining at a constant level or rate, without speeding up or slowing down
senses.definitionCN: 保持在恒定水平或速率上，不快也不慢
senses.example: A falling object moves in nearly uniform acceleration near the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 落体在地面附近几乎做匀加速运动。
senses.why: In physics one form must also mean one rate: nothing in the motion changes shape.
senses.whyCN: 在物理学里，一种形式也要求一种速率：运动中没有任何部分改变样子。

senses.title: To make things alike
senses.definition: to bring parts or rules into one form, so that all are alike
senses.definitionCN: 把各部分或规则归成一种形式，使它们彼此相同
senses.example: The new manager uniformed the labels across the whole warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 新任经理把整个仓库的标签统一了起来。
senses.why: The verb turns the state into an action: someone decides what the one form shall be.
senses.whyCN: 动词把状态变成动作：由某个人来决定那唯一的形式是什么。

senses.title: Members of the service
senses.definition: used with the to mean the police, soldiers, or other people in uniform
senses.definitionCN: 与 the 连用，指警察、士兵或其他穿制服的人
senses.example: The crowd stepped aside quickly when the uniform arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 穿制服的人一到，人群立刻让开。
senses.why: By a familiar shift, the clothing stands for whoever wears it.
senses.whyCN: 衣服代替了穿它的人，这是常见的转义。

intro.en: Uniform joins a Latin word for one to a Latin word for shape, and the pair entered English through French.
intro.cn: uniform 把拉丁语表示「一」的词与表示「形状」的词拼在一起，再经由法语进入英语。

items.en: Unus meant one, and forma meant a shape, mould, or appearance.
items.cn: 拉丁语 unus 意为「一」，forma 意为「形状、模子、外观」。

items.en: Uniformis was used for what keeps a single form, and the schools applied it to evenness of quality.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 uniformis 指保持单一形式的事物，经院学者用它表示质性齐一。

items.en: French uniforme carried both the abstract sense of even and same and, later, the sense of a dress.
items.cn: 法语 uniforme 既有「一律、相同」的抽象义，后来又生出了服装义。

items.en: From the seventeenth century soldiers and servants were dressed alike, and uniform came to mean the dress itself.
items.cn: 十七世纪起士兵与仆役制服整齐，uniform 由此转指这套衣服。

items.en: Schools, hospitals and transport staff adopted uniforms, while science kept the sense of uniform speed and uniform law.
items.cn: 学校、医院与交通部门采用制服，科学界则保留匀速与统一规律的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on uni- and forma; the near-meaning group gathers words for clothing and for sameness with different emphasis.
note.cn: 形近组收以 uni- 与 forma 构成的词；近义组收表示服装与一致性的词，侧重点不同。

entries.definition: The noun for being the same everywhere; the quality behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一致性、一律」，是形容词背后的性质。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in the same way everywhere, or at an even rate.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「一致地、均匀地」。

entries.definition: An adjective for someone who is wearing a uniform.
To make separate parts into one whole; it shares the one part but not the shape.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「统一、使成一体」，共享「一」这一部分而非形状。

entries.definition: A shape or a printed paper; the second half of uniform on its own.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「形状、表格」，即 uniform 的后半部分。

entries.definition: Always the same in behaviour or standard; usually about actions rather than looks.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「一贯的、一致的」，多指行为或标准而非外观。

entries.definition: An agreed level or pattern that things should meet.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「标准」，指应达到的既定水平或样式。

entries.definition: A set of clothes worn together, with no idea of group membership.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一套衣服」，不含团体属含义。

entries.definition: The distinctive dress given to servants or staff of a household.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「号衣、仆役制服」，历史上大户人家发给仆人的服装。

entries.definition: An official rule, or the plain clothing required by one, as in regulation dress.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「规定」，也可指规定所要求的朴素服装。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two Latin pieces, one and form, and the ordinary phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用两个拉丁部件「一」与「形」，以及这个词常用的搭配。

normal.en: Uni- means one and form means shape: one shape of clothing for everyone.
normal.cn: uni- 表示「一」，form 表示「形状」：所有人只穿一种形状的衣服。

normal.en: School uniform, military uniform, in uniform: the phrase always marks belonging.
normal.cn: school uniform、military uniform、in uniform：这些搭配都在标记归属。

normal.en: Uniform rules and uniform speed keep one form across space and time.
normal.cn: 统一规则与匀速运动都在空间与时间上保持同一形式。

normal.en: Uniform is also a physics word, as in uniform motion.
normal.cn: uniform 也是物理术语，如匀速运动 uniform motion。

normal.en: The uniform can stand for the person: the crowd quietened when the uniform came.
normal.cn: 制服可以代替人：制服一到，人群就安静了。

abstract.en: Picture many shoulders under cloth cut once: the individual is still there, but the outline is shared.
abstract.cn: 想象许多肩膀罩在同一块剪裁好的布下：个人还在，轮廓却是共享的。

abstract.en: A uniform is a promise made visible: whoever wears it agrees to be seen as one of a group.
abstract.cn: 制服是看得见的承诺：谁穿上它，就同意被看作团体中的一员。

abstract.en: From clothes to rules to speed, the word always asks whether everything really has the same shape.
abstract.cn: 从服装到规则再到速度，这个词始终在问：所有东西真的都是同一个形状吗。

examples.en: He keeps his old army uniform folded in a wooden box.
examples.cn: 他把旧军装叠好放在一只木箱里。

examples.en: The two schools agreed on a uniform exam paper.
examples.cn: 两所学校商定使用统一的试卷。

examples.en: The train moved at a uniform speed along the straight track.
examples.cn: 列车沿笔直的轨道匀速前进。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优尼佛姆」——优尼一人一件佛姆款：统一的制服

root: 源自拉丁语 unus「一」加 forma「形状」，中世纪拉丁语 uniformis 指「保持单一形式、性质齐一」，经法语 uniforme 进入英语，十七世纪起转指统一的服装，科学中也保留「匀速、统一规律」的用法。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of uniform all hold one idea: a single shape imposed on many things, whether clothes, rules, speed, labels, or the people who wear them.
sensesIntro.cn: uniform 的五个义项都守住同一个观念：把单一的形状施加到许多对象上，无论那是衣服、规则、速度、标签，还是穿它的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of students in identical blue clothes with identical buttons.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排学生穿着同样的蓝色衣服，纽扣也一模一样。

branches.en: THE CLOTHES: one cut of cloth worn by a whole group.
branches.cn: 服装线：一整个团体都穿同一种剪裁的布。

branches.en: THE RULES: the same standard applied everywhere without exception.
branches.cn: 规则线：同一标准被无例外地用到处处。

branches.en: THE RATE: in physics the form and the speed must stay one.
branches.cn: 速率线：在物理中形式与速度都必须保持同一。

branches.en: THE ACT: someone brings parts into the one form.
branches.cn: 动作线：由某人把各部分归入那唯一的形式。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: the clothing stands for the person who wears it.
branches.cn: 人物线：衣服代替了穿衣服的人。

intro.en: Uniform is a Latin prefix-root pair with an English suffix family grown on top.
intro.cn: uniform 是一对拉丁语前缀与词根，上面又长出一族英语后缀词。

latinIntro.en: Both unus and forma are recorded Latin words, and uniformis is recorded in medieval Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 unus 与 forma 都有文献记录，uniformis 见于中世纪拉丁语。

items.example: The prefix supplies the idea of oneness.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀提供「唯一」的意思。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of shape.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「形状」的意思。

items.example: The Latin source of the second half.
items.exampleCN: 后半部分的拉丁语来源。

items.example: The recorded Latin form of the whole word.
items.exampleCN: 整词在中世纪拉丁语中的形式。

items.example: A cousin built on the same prefix.
items.exampleCN: 用同一前缀构成的近亲词。

definition_zh: 联合；结合；工会；联盟；同盟；团结
definition_en: the joining of separate parts into one, or an organization formed by such a joining
core_image: 两只手握在一起，指尖扣得紧紧的
scene: 十几家小作坊的师傅在一张桌前签下同一份章程，从此一起谈价钱。The craftsmen formed a union to protect their trade.
sceneCN: 这里 union 是「工会」（第 2 个义项：由联合而成的组织）；句意为工匠们结成了一个行会来维护本行。两只紧握的手，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「联合；团结」
同根名词，义为「团结；统一」
动词加 -ed 的形容词，义为「联合的；一致的」
同根动词，义为「统一；使一致」

senses.title: The act of joining into one
senses.definition: the joining of two or more things so that they become one
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或更多事物结合成一体的过程
senses.example: The bridge is a happy union of steel and glass.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥是钢与玻璃的巧妙结合。
senses.why: The Latin unus, one, plus the noun ending io, gives the idea of making one out of several.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 unus（一）加名词词尾 io，给出「把多个变成一」的意思。

senses.title: An organization of workers
senses.definition: an organization of employees who act together over pay and conditions
senses.definitionCN: 为工资与工作条件共同行动的雇员组织
senses.example: The union asked for a shorter working week.
senses.exampleCN: 工会要求缩短每周工作时间。
senses.why: Workers who speak with one voice are joined into one body, and the body takes the name.
senses.whyCN: 用一个声音说话的工人被联结成一个整体，而这个整体直接取得了这个名字。

senses.title: A league of states or groups
senses.definition: a political or trade alliance in which separate parts keep some of their own powers
senses.definitionCN: 各部分保留部分自主权的政治或经济联盟
senses.example: The two countries signed a customs union in 1957.
senses.exampleCN: 两国在 1957 年签订了一个关税同盟。
senses.why: Joining for a purpose without melting completely is the political version of the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 为了某个目的结合而不完全融为一体，是同一幅画面的政治版本。

senses.title: Harmony between people
senses.definition: a state of agreement and love between people or within a group
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间或群体内部的和谐与情谊
senses.example: The couple lived in union for fifty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这对夫妻和睦地生活了五十年。
senses.why: When separate lives hold together, the union is a bond rather than an institution.
senses.whyCN: 当各自的生活握在一起，这个 union 就是一种纽带，而不是机构。

senses.title: A place where students gather
senses.definition: used in names of student organizations or their buildings
senses.definitionCN: 用于学生组织或其活动场所的名称
senses.example: They met at the student union and planned the concert.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在学生会见面，筹划了那场音乐会。
senses.why: A building named after the joining of students is simply the institution turned into a place.
senses.whyCN: 以学生之联合命名的场所，不过是把机构变成了具体的地方。

intro.en: The word goes back to Latin unio, oneness, from unus, one.
intro.cn: 这个词可追到拉丁语 unio（一体），源自 unus（一）。

items.en: Unio meant oneness, and also named a single large pearl.
items.cn: unio 意为「一体」，也指一颗大珍珠。

items.en: The word entered French as union with the sense of combining.
items.cn: 该词进入法语作 union，含「结合」之义。

items.en: English used union for the joining of things, people, and realms.
items.cn: 英语用 union 表示物、人与人乃至王国的结合。

items.en: From the eighteenth century it named associations of workers or traders.
items.cn: 十八世纪起，它用来指工人或商人的组织。

items.en: In politics it appears in the names of alliances and federal states.
items.cn: 在政治中，它出现于联盟与联邦国家的名称里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers uni- words, and the near-meaning group covers leagues and harmony.
note.cn: 形近组收集 uni- 开头的词，近义组覆盖联盟与和谐的说法。

the state of being one
one shared dress
a round vegetable with layers
entries.definitionCN: 洋葱（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

an organized group of people
a group of teams or states
the act of splitting apart

normalIntro.en: One root, one, sits under the union, the unit, and the united.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示「一」的词根，撑起 union、unit 与 united。

normal.en: Uni- is one, and -ion makes a noun of the joining.
normal.cn: uni- 是「一」，-ion 把这种结合变作名词。

normal.en: Trade union is the British phrase; labor union is the American one.
normal.cn: trade union 是英式说法，labor union 是美式说法。

normal.en: Unity is the state, union is the act or the body.
normal.cn: unity 是状态，union 是行为或那个实体。

normal.en: United appears in country names that grew out of unions.
normal.cn: 许多国家名里的 united 正出自这样的联合。

normal.en: The same root gives unit, unite, and unique.
normal.cn: 同一个词根还生出 unit、unite 与 unique。

abstract.en: Picture two hands clasped with fingers locked.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手指紧扣的手。

abstract.en: See dozens of small workshops putting one stamp on a single sheet.
abstract.cn: 看几十家小作坊在同一张纸上盖下同一个印。

abstract.en: Hear a hall of voices agreeing on a single sentence.
abstract.cn: 听满厅的声音在同一句话上达成一致。

examples.en: The union of the two firms created the largest bank in the region.
examples.cn: 两家公司的合并造就了本地区最大的银行。

examples.en: Union members voted to accept the new pay offer.
examples.cn: 工会会员投票接受了新的薪酬方案。

examples.en: Their marriage was a union of two very different families.
examples.cn: 他们的婚姻是两个差异极大的家庭的结合。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尤尼昂」——尤尼（一）加昂（上），大家往一个方向上凑，就是联合。

root: 拉丁语 unus（一）+ 名词词尾 -io 构成 unio（一体），经古法语 union 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One root, one, gives the act of joining, the body formed, the league, the bond, and the building.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个表示「一」的词根，给出结合的行为、形成的实体、联盟、纽带与场所。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands clasped with fingers locked.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手指紧扣的手。

branches.en: The act branch: things joined into a new whole.
branches.cn: 行为分支：事物联结成新的整体。

branches.en: The workers branch: one voice for many employees.
branches.cn: 劳工分支：众多雇员共用一个声音。

branches.en: The state branch: separate parts under one flag.
branches.cn: 国家分支：各部分共处一面旗帜之下。

branches.en: The bond branch: lives held together in harmony.
branches.cn: 纽带分支：和谐中相依的生活。

branches.en: The place branch: a building named after the joining.
branches.cn: 场所分支：以这种联合命名的建筑。

intro.en: The word is a Latin number plus a noun ending, carried through French.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语数词加名词词尾，经由法语传来。

latinIntro.en: Unus and unio are the Latin sources, and uni- recurs across the family.
latinIntro.cn: unus 与 unio 是拉丁语来源，uni- 在这一族里反复出现。

items.example: Union names the act of making one.
items.exampleCN: union 指合而为一的行为。

items.example: Unity names the state of being one.
Alliance and union are near twins.
items.exampleCN: alliance 与 union 是近邻。

items.example: A league of towns met each spring.
items.exampleCN: 各镇组成的联盟每年春天集会。
